General surveys of a parent technology are 0. AI assistant, from the topic, the full title and the first 220 characters of `abstract` (the rule's rescue reads all of it), in a shuffled order (seed 20261022), blind to every rule decision. Both splits were labelled on 2026-10-22; only dev was read.

rows.title: A review on application of activated carbons for carbon dioxide capture: present performance, preparation, and surface modification for further improvement.
rows.abstract: The atmosphere security and regulation of climate change are being continuously highlighted as a pressing issue. The crisis of climate change owing to the anthropogenic carbon dioxide emission has led many governments at federal and provincial levels to promulgate policies to address this concern. Among them is regulating the carbon dioxide emission from major industrial sources such as power plants, petrochemical industries, cement plants, and other industries that depend on the combustion of fossil fuels for energy to operate. In view of this, various CO2 capture and sequestration technologies have been investigated and presented. From this review, adsorption of CO2 on porous solid materials has been gaining increasing attention due to its cost-effectiveness, ease of application, and comparably low energy demand. Despite the myriad of advanced materials such as zeolites, carbons-based, metal-organic frameworks, mesoporous silicas, and polymers being researched, research on activated carbons (ACs) continue to be in the mainstream. Therefore, this review is endeavored to elucidate the adsorption properties of CO2 on activated carbons derived from different sources. Selective adsorption based on pore size/shape and surface chemistry is investigated. Accordingly, the effect of surface modifications of the ACs with NH3, amines, and metal oxides on adsorption performance toward CO2 is evaluated. The adsorption performance of the activated carbons under humid conditions is also reviewed. Finally, activated carbon-based composite has been surveyed and recommended as a feasible strategy to improve AC adsorption properties toward CO2. The activated carbon surface in the graphical abstract is nitrogen rich modified using ammonia through thermal treatment. The values of CO2 emissions by sources are taken from (Yoro and Daramola 2020).

rows.title: Advanced oxidation pretreatment of biomass for preparation of carbon-based adsorbents with high CO2 capture performance
Amine-Site Accessibility and Low-Temperature Deep-Vacuum Regeneration of Biomass-Derived Porous Carbons for Direct Air Capture
rows.abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) with supported amines depends on reversible CO2–amine interactions within a confined phase, so working capacity is governed by both access to the amine-containing phase and regeneration conditions. In this study, tetraethylenepentamine (TEPA)- and polyethylenimine (PEI)-functionalized biomass-derived porous carbons were evaluated in a fixed-bed system at 500 ppm CO2. TEPA samples showed substantially higher amine-mass-normalized uptake than PEI at comparable loading, indicating more favorable adsorption-transport behavior under the fixed-bed conditions. TEP-30 and TEP-40 reached 0.38–0.39 mmol g−1 under dry atmospheric-pressure conditions. Increasing the adsorption pressure to 0.2 MPa(g) raised the TEP-30 capacity to 0.58 mmol g−1. Regeneration at 110 °C caused rapid capacity loss, whereas vacuum alone at 500 Pa was insufficient. Coupling 80 °C with 500 Pa improved short-term cyclic working-capacity retention under the tested cycles by combining thermal activation of desorption with a low gas-phase CO2 chemical potential. The results establish a reaction–transport framework for interpreting supported-amine DAC and demonstrate the potential of moderate-temperature, deep-vacuum regeneration under the tested fixed-bed cycles.

rows.title: Biomass-Based N-Rich Porous Carbon Materials for CO2 Capture and in-situ Conversion.
rows.abstract: Capturing CO2 and subsequently converting into valuable chemicals has attracted extensive attention. Herein, a series of biomass-based N-rich porous carbon materials with high specific surface area and pore volume were prepared using biomass waste soybean dregs as precursors. The nitrogen content was up to 4 % with different forms in the carbon skeleton such as pyridine-N, pyrrole-N. The synergistic effect of ultra-micropore (pore size <0.7 nm) and N-containing groups endowed the materials with a high CO2 adsorption capacity, reaching 6.3 and 3.6 mmol g-1 at 0 and 25 °C under atmospheric pressure, respectively. In addition, the sufficient interaction between N-containing groups and CO2 was demonstrated by solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and the captured CO2 was possibly activated in the form of carbamate, which is conducive to subsequent conversion. Therefore, the supported catalyst with the as-synthetic porous carbon material as the carrier and ZnII as catalytic sites was prepared and successfully applied for carboxylative cyclization of propargylic amine with CO2 to afford the 3-benzyl-5-methyleneoxazolidin-2-one. The results showed that CO2 capture and in-situ conversion work effectively to produce highly value-added chemicals. In this process, the captured CO2 could be activated and fixed into chemicals in mild conditions. More importantly, the energy consumption in CO2 desorption and adsorbent regeneration could be avoided. The valorization of both solid waste and CO2 to valuable chemicals provides an elegant strategy of killing three birds with one stone.

rows.title: Carbon-Based Adsorbents for Postcombustion CO2 Capture: A Critical Review.
rows.abstract: The persistent increase in atmospheric CO2 from anthropogenic sources makes research directed toward carbon capture and storage imperative. Current liquid amine absorption technology has several drawbacks including hazardous byproducts and a high-energy requirement for regeneration; therefore, research is ongoing to develop more practical methods for capturing CO2 in postcombustion scenarios. The unique properties of carbon-based materials make them specifically promising for CO2 adsorption at low temperature and moderate to high partial pressure. This critical review aims to highlight the development of carbon-based solid sorbents for postcombustion CO2 capture. Specifically, it provides an overview of postcombustion CO2 capture processes with solid adsorbents and discusses a variety of carbon-based materials that could be used. This review focuses on low-cost pyrogenic carbon, activated carbon (AC), and metal-carbon composites for CO2 capture. Further, it touches upon the recent progress made to develop metal organic frameworks (MOFs) and carbon nanomaterials and their general CO2 sorption potential.

rows.title: Carbon dioxide capture coupled with magnesium utilization from seawater by bipolar membrane electrodialysis.
rows.abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) capture coupled with further mineralization in high value-added form is a great challenge for carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) processes. In this work, a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) technique integrated with crystallization chamber was proposed to utilize CO2-derived carbonates and the residual magnesium resource from seawater to produce functional nesquehonite. To ensure the stable CO2 storage and magnesium extraction by BMED process, the metastable zone during nesquehonite crystallizing was first measured to modulate crystallization rate, obtain high-quality crystal products and inhibit membrane fouling states. Subsequently, the effects of current density, temperature, and CO2 flow rate during the whole BMED-crystallization process were further investigated. The increase in current density and temperature was conducive for the extraction of magnesium while the enlarged gas flow rate induced higher absorption of CO2. Under the current density at 22 A/m2, CO2 flow rate at 50 mL/min and temperature at 30 °C, the optimal carbon absorption ratio and the magnesium extraction ratio reached 50.85% and 56.71%, respectively. Under this condition, the explosion nucleation of the nesquehonite was effectively avoided to inhibit membrane fouling and the generation of magnesium hydroxide was depressed to obtain the target product nesquehonite. This study on simultaneous carbon capture and magnesium utilization provides theoretical guidance for the industrial green storage of CO2 and development of valuable magnesium products.

rows.title: Carbon dioxide capture with aqueous calcium carbide residual solution for calcium carbonate synthesis and its use as an epoxy resin filler.
rows.abstract: Calcium carbide residue (CCR) is a waste obtained from the production of acetylene gas by the hydration reaction of calcium carbide. This residue is generated in large quantities annually and requires appropriate disposal. The main composition of the residue is calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2). Ca(OH)2 can react with CO2 gas and form CaCO3 particles. This process is well known but not very attractive since Ca(OH)2 is obtained from limestone using an energy-intensive thermal conversion process. This paper examined the synthesis of CaCO3 from CCR solutions by capturing CO2 with the aid of triethanolamine (TEA) solutions at doses of 0, 5, 10 and 20% w/w. The precipitated CaCO3 was characterized, and the application of CaCO3 as a filler in epoxy resin was tested. The results showed that the precipitated CaCO3 was mainly calcite, with a 76.6% yield. Cubic calcite was primarily obtained in TEA solutions, whereas small and agglomerated spherical vaterite and cubic calcite particles were formed in non-TEA solutions. The CaCO3-filled epoxy composites showed higher compressive strength than the neat resin. However, the transparency of specimen plates was reduced. These results can serve as guidelines for the application of CCR slurry filtrate obtained from the sedimentation ponds of acetylene plants and help to reduce the amount of wastewater that needs to be treated. CO2 gas from industrial flue gas combined with TEA solution could be applied to precipitate CaCO3 for carbon-neutral manufacturing.

rows.title: Carbon Farming as an Emerging Agribusiness: Markets, Business Models, Risks and Farmer Value Capture
rows.abstract: Carbon farming is increasingly presented as a means of rewarding land managers for storing carbon, reducing agricultural greenhouse gas emissions and supplying differentiated environmental attributes to buyers. Its agribusiness viability, however, cannot be inferred from biophysical mitigation potential or the existence of tradable credits. This critical narrative review integrates research on soil carbon science, environmental economics, contract design, voluntary carbon markets, farmer behaviour and agricultural value-chain governance. Peer-reviewed evidence and relevant institutional frameworks published through 9 August 2026 were examined with particular attention to methodological strength, conflicting findings and distributional outcomes. The synthesis distinguishes carbon removals from emission reductions, carbon-credit sales from value-chain payments, and gross revenue from the value ultimately retained by farmers. Empirical studies suggest that measurement uncertainty, counterfactual design, reversal exposure, fragmented holdings and costly verification constrain the conversion of agronomic improvements into reliable marketable units. Farmer surveys and choice experiments repeatedly identify delayed payment, repayment liability, unclear terms, data-sharing concerns and uncertainty about additionality as barriers, although stated preferences are not equivalent to observed adoption. Case evidence from Europe, Australia, India, Kenya and the United States shows that finance structure and control over credit rights can matter as much as headline prices for farmer benefit. Action-based, outcome-based and hybrid contracts allocate risks differently, while aggregation offers potential bargaining advantages without guaranteed cost savings or equitable distribution. The review develops a conditional value-capture framework centred on auditable environmental claims, transparent net-revenue accounting, farmer-controlled options, proportionate risk sharing and independent dispute resolution. It concludes that carbon farming can become a complementary agribusiness activity under credible measurement and inclusive governance, but cannot currently be assumed to deliver dependable stand-alone farm income or interchangeable offsets across practices and locations. Priority research needs concern longitudinal net farm returns, independent verification of environmental outcomes and comparative tests of contract and ownership arrangements.

rows.title: Carbon Support–Alkali Interplay Controls CO₂ Slip during Direct Air Capture and Methanation over Dual-Functional Materials
Code and simulated data for bounded-error certification of integrated carbon dioxide capture under analyser dynamics
rows.abstract: Reproducibility release for the simulation-based study of bounded-error certification of integrated carbon dioxide capture. The fixed partitioned LP enclosure retains shared analyser offsets, response parameters and gas-balance constraints across complete records. The archive preserves the 384-record confirmation, independent calibration records, signed-mean tests on 96 Reference A and 96 new Reference B records, 32 longer-record MHE comparisons and 60 drift settings on 20 paired cases. It contains source, simulated observations and labels, calibration scores, raw posterior capture draws, LP and MHE-arrival dual multipliers, nonlinear histories, retrospective target-membership diagnostics, numerical checks and a cryptographic inventory. Both process references were developed within this project. All dynamic evaluation is simulated. Version 1.9.0 corrects presentation and cross-references without changing evaluated numerical results. Original personal historical uploads are excluded. MIT applies to original code and simulated data; manuscript text and third-party materials retain their respective copyrights.

rows.title: Corrosion behavior and interfacial mechanism of 20# carbon steel in a non-aqueous [AEP][Pro]-ethanol absorbent for CO2 capture
Decision letter for "Biogenic carbon for thermally regenerable CO₂ capture"
Development and CO2 capture of nitrogen-enriched microporous carbon by coupling waste polyamides with lignocellulosic biomass.
rows.abstract: Due to the substantial emissions of global CO2, there has been growing interest in nitrogen-enriched porous carbonaceous materials that possess exceptional CO2 capture capabilities. In this study, a novel N-enriched microporous carbon was synthesized by integrating waste polyamides with lignocellulosic biomass, involving carbonization and physicochemical activation. As-synthesized adsorbents demonstrated significant characteristics including a high specific surface area (1710 m2/g) and a large micropore volume (0.497 cm3/g), as well as abundant N- and O-containing functional groups, achieved through activation at 700 °C. They displayed remarkable CO2 capture capability, achieving uptake levels of up to 6.71 mmol/g at 1 bar and 0 °C, primarily due to the filling effect of narrow micropore along with electrostatic interaction. Furthermore, the adsorbent exhibited a rapid capacity for CO2 capture, achieving 94.9% of its saturation capacity within a mere 5 min at 30 °C. This impressive performance was accurately described by the pseudo second-order dynamic model. Additionally, as-synthesized adsorbents displayed a moderate isosteric heat of CO2 adsorption, as well as superior selectivity over N2. Even after undergoing five consecutive cycles, it maintained ∼100% of its initial capacity. Undoubtedly, such findings hold immense significance in the mitigation of global plastic pollution and greenhouse effect.

rows.title: Direct Photo- and Electrothermally Regenerable Adsorbents for Carbon Dioxide Capture Using Conjugated Metal−Organic Frameworks
rows.abstract: Adsorbent regeneration in carbon dioxide capture systems primarily relies on external temperature and pressure swings, posing critical challenges of intensive energy penalties and low cycling rates. Here we demonstrate a direct photo- and electrothermal swing method for CO 2 capture using two-dimensional conjugated MOF Cu 3 (2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) 2 (Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 ) and its derivatives. Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 releases CO 2 captured at room-temperature through photo- or electrothermal effects by directly applying one-sun irradiation or a voltage of 10 V. The capture-release process operates across 1%-50% CO 2 with a cyclic frequency of 4-5 h -1 and adsorption capacities of 0.04-1.11 mmol g -1 . Incorporating alkylamine groups into Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 further enhances CO 2 adsorption capacity by more than three-fold, with corresponding energy consumptions down to 145 and 60 kJ mol -1 for 1% and 10% CO 2 , respectively, via photothermal regeneration. Structurally integrating energy conversion functions and CO 2 adsorption sites within a single, porous material establishes a new blueprint for solar-driven and electrified carbon management.

rows.title: Driving factors of carbon emissions in China’s marine capture fisheries (2015-2024) based on LMDI model
rows.abstract: Marine capture fisheries are an important source of carbon emissions in China’s marine economy. This study estimates carbon emissions from China’s marine capture fisheries during 2015-2024. The Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method is used to examine the driving factors. Carbon emissions declined from 5.435 million metric tons in 2015 to 4.99 million metric tons in 2024. A small increase appeared after 2022. The overall trend remained downward. The LMDI results show that labor force and industrial scale reduced carbon emissions. Energy intensity increased carbon emissions. Previous studies mainly examined total carbon emissions in the marine fisheries sector. Previous studies also focused on general driving factors. This study examines the marine capture fisheries sector only. The analysis reveals a change from scale-driven decarbonization to efficiency-driven decarbonization.

rows.title: Effective CO2 capture by in-situ nitrogen-doped nanoporous carbon derived from waste antibiotic fermentation residues.
rows.abstract: It is of great environmental benefit to rationally dispose of and utilize antibiotic fermentation residues. In this study, oxytetracycline fermentation residue was transformed into an in-situ nitrogen-doped nanoporous carbon material with high CO2 adsorption performance by low-temperature pyrolysis pre-carbonization coupled with pyrolytic activation. The results indicated the activation under mild conditions (600 °C, KOH/OC = 2) was able to increase micropores and reduce the loss of in-situ nitrogen content. The developed microporous structure was beneficial for the filling adsorption of CO2, and the in-situ nitrogen doping in a high oxygen-containing carbon framework also strengthened the electrostatic adsorption with CO2. The maximum CO2 adsorption reached 4.38 mmol g-1 and 6.40 mmol g-1 at 25 °C and 0 °C (1 bar), respectively, with high CO2/N2 selectivity (32/1) and excellent reusability (decreased by 4% after 5 cycles). This study demonstrates the good application potential of oxytetracycline fermentation residue as in-situ nitrogen-doped nanoporous carbon materials for CO2 capture.

rows.title: Efficient capture of radioactive iodine by ZIF-8 derived porous carbon.
rows.abstract: Due to the rapid diffusion of radioactive iodine, the demand for safe and efficient capture and storage of radioactive iodine is increasing worldwide. The use of porous carbon materials to capture iodine has aroused great interest. This work prepared porous carbon materials derived from polymetallic oxides of the zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) by pyrolysis at 1000 °C. The carbon materials (CZIF-1000) have a high specific surface area of about 1110 m2/g and a total pore volume of 0.92 cm3/g. Adsorption studies have shown that the CZIF-1000 had significant adsorption performance for iodine, and the adsorption capacity can reach 790.8 mg/g at 8h. The potential mechanism of adsorption is that the carbonization causes the charge-transfer interaction and pore size distribution. Compared with the conventional adsorbents, the adsorbents showed faster kinetics and high extraction capacity for iodine. This experiment provides an effective method for designing a highly efficient adsorbent for iodine and broadens the ideas for developing new iodine extraction adsorbents.

rows.title: Feasibility of Upcycling Spent Lithium-ion Battery to Carbon Dioxide Capture Adsorbent
rows.abstract: This study investigates the feasibility of repurposing spent lithium-ion battery (SLIB) to lithium orthosilicate (Li4SiO4), a high temperature carbon dioxide sorbent. Two synthesis pathways including conventional acid-leaching method (Scenario 1) and a pyrolysis-based route (Scenario 2) were explored. Additionally, techno-economic analysis (TEA) and lifecycle assessment (LCA) of the two processes were also performed. Different analytical characterization techniques were performed to understand the material properties of Li4SiO4 including surface area, crystallinity, morphology and thermal stability. CO2 capture performance of the synthesized Li4SiO4 was tested in a thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA) using dynamic, isothermal and cyclic methods. Dynamic test shows the adsorption-desorption peak temperatures of 602oC and 500oC for the leaching-based and pyrolysis-based sorbents respectively. The material produced from Scenario 1 had an isothermal CO2 capture capacity ranging from 0.10 – 0.27 g CO2/ g of sorbent. On the contrary, Scenario 2 had a higher adsorption capacity ranging from 0.18 – 0.33 g CO2/ g of sorbent. Over 10 cycles, cyclic CO2 capture was performed for about 1500 min using the leaching-based and pyrolysis-based sorbents, showing that an adsorption potential of 99.5% was consistently maintained by scenario 1’s sorbent, while scenario 2 experienced a drastic decline in adsorption rate with 88% as its lowest. The TEA shows that Scenario 1 yields a minimum selling price (MSP) of US$ 3.49/kg and a payback period (PBP) of ≈ 2 years and 10 months, while Scenario 2 results in an MSP of US$ 3.65/kg and a PBP of ≈ 3 years. Both pathways are economically feasible. However, Scenario 1 demonstrates a lower production cost and higher net present value under base-case assumptions.

rows.title: Particle size-dependent carbon source capture and carbon allocation pathways by activated sludge
rows.abstract: Capturing organic carbon source from municipal wastewater by activated sludge is a key strategy to support energy self-sufficiency in treatment plants. In practical applications, the carbon source capture efficiency of activated sludge is often limited. Variations in particle size can lead to differences in microbial activity and metabolic pathways within activated sludge. These changes further affect the content and composition of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), ultimately influencing its capacity to capture carbon sources. Mixed activated sludge was separated into fractions with particle sizes of 500, 250, 176, 133, and 88 μm to examine how particle size affects the capture efficiency of different forms of carbon sources. It was observed that carbon source capture performance was strongly influenced by sludge particle size, with smaller particles showing higher capture capacity. The activated sludge with a particle size of 88 μm achieved a tCOD capture efficiency of 65.95%, which is 35.95 percentage points higher than that of the 500 μm group. Adsorption and intracellular storage played dominant roles in the capture pathways. With decreasing particle size, hydrophobic interactions increased, while electrostatic repulsion weakened, lowering the energy barrier for microbial aggregation with carbon substrates. Flow cytometry and fractal analysis suggest that smaller sludge fractions contain more viable bacteria and form flocs with more irregular structures and larger surface areas. This study quantitatively links five sludge particle-size fractions with the capture of different COD forms and their carbon allocation pathways, and identified 88-133 μm as a favorable particle-size range for carbon source capture under the tested conditions. These findings provide a mechanistic and operational basis for regulating sludge particle-size distribution toward optimizing front-end carbon capture in wastewater treatment plants.

rows.title: Progress in carbon dioxide separation and capture: a review.
rows.abstract: This article reviews the progress made in CO2 separation and capture research and engineering. Various technologies, such as absorption, adsorption, and membrane separation, are thoroughly discussed. New concepts such as chemical-looping combustion and hydrate-based separation are also introduced briefly. Future directions are suggested. Sequestration methods, such as forestation, ocean fertilization and mineral carbonation techniques are also covered. Underground injection and direct ocean dump are not covered.

rows.title: Solving two environmental problems simultaneously：Microporous carbon derived from mixed plastic waste for CO2 capture.
rows.abstract: Conversion of plastic waste into porous carbon for CO2 capture is an attractive approach to solve the carbon emission and plastic pollution problems, simultaneously. However, the previous studies are limited to the utilization of single PET plastic. The conversion of mixed plastic waste (MPW), which is of more practical significance, is seldom reported. In this study, mixed plastic waste was converted into porous carbon materials for CO2 capture through cascading autogenic pressure carbonization (APC) and chemical activation. The carbon yield of 56% was achieved through APC of MPW. The activator (KOH) dosage had significant effects on the structure and properties of the prepared porous carbons. Porous carbon prepared with KOH/C ratio of 4 had the largest micropore area and the maximum CO2 adsorption was 2.7 mmol g-1 at 298 K and 1 bar. The experimental data were well fitted to the pesudo first-order kinetic model. The MPW derived porous carbon exhibited not only high CO2 uptake capacity, but also fast adsorption rate, good selectivity of CO2 over N2 and good cyclic stability, which could be regarded as a promising adsorbent for CO2 adsorption.

rows.title: Structure – Performance relationship of tertiary amines for CO2 Capture & Carbon Mineralization (CCMC)
rows.abstract: The amine-based CO 2 capture & mineral carbonation (CCMC) using alkaline slag represents a promising decarbonation strategy. While prior studies have shown the type of amine as a critical factor for CO 2 absorption and mineralization kinetics, their molecular structural effects remain underexplored. This work combines experiments with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically investigate the structure–performance relationship of tertiary amines in coupled CO 2 capture and mineral carbonation, focusing on calcium conversion, apparent mineralization kinetics, and CaCO 3 product characteristics to inform rational amine selection and design. Specially, this work evaluates how selected properties of tertiary amine structures, i.e., length of the carbon chain, number of hydroxyl and amine groups, presence cyclic frameworks, impact CCMC efficiency. Experimental and quantum chemical analyses reveal that the apparent CCMC rate generally increased with amine basicity. Within the TREA–DEEA–EDEA–TEA series, increasing hydroxyl substitution decreased proton affinity, initial solution pH, and calcium-conversion rate. While steric hindrance and hydrogen bonding show negligible impacts. Surprisingly, the presence of additional amine groups does not boost reactivity due to unfavorable secondary protonation energetics. Interestingly, the interactive energy term proton affinity showed a broad correlation with the apparent calcium-conversion trend for elucidating the amine property – performance relationship in CO 2 capture. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing tertiary amines to optimize carbon capture kinetics and product purity, with implications for scalable industrial deployment.

rows.title: Thermal Source Compatibility Limits for Temperature-Vacuum Swing Adsorption Direct Air Capture: Finite Power, Heat Transfer, and Exergy Constraints for Low-Carbon Thermal Integration
rows.abstract: Temperature-vacuum swing adsorption (TVSA) direct air capture (DAC) is often modelled with a prescribed regeneration-wall temperature, which does not identify the thermal source capability required to realise it. This study replaces that boundary with a finite heat source defined by temperature, maximum thermal power, and source-to-wall conductance, with desorption pressure treated as an interacting process variable. A dynamic wall balance distinguishes source heat, wall-to-bed transfer, wall sensible heating, and source-to-wall irreversibility. For the selected APDES contactor under the fixed reference cycle, a 120 °C wall temperature limit, nominally zero external regeneration heat loss, and a desorption pressure of 0.073 bar, the conditional source-power boundary is approximately 4.2–4.3 kWmbed−3 over 120–160 °C, while the conductance boundary decreases from approximately 135 to 48 W mbed−3K−1. These limits are not jointly sufficient: at 130 °C, the minimum feasible conductance decreases from approximately 247 to 82 W mbed−3 K−1 as the power density rises from approximately 4.2 to 8.4 kWmbed−3. Near-equivalent performance requires approximately 14.23 MJ kg−1 CO2 of source heat, while thermal exergy increases from 3.62 to 4.60 MJ kg−1 CO2 between 120 and 160 °C. The resulting 187-point process envelope supports the screening of solar thermal, thermal energy storage, waste heat, and other low-carbon heat supplies for DAC integration.

rows.title: Thermally engineered ER-Fc-MOF@foam carbon monoliths for polyethylene microplastic remediation: Integrating interfacial capture with Fenton-like oxidative transformation
A cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
A multimodal measurement and data fusion framework for estimating power transformer insulation condition using heterogeneous sensor systems
A Novel Power Quality Confidence Evaluation Method for Microgrid Cluster Based on the Fusion of Bootstrap and Hoeffding’s Inequality
A Thermal-Aware Infrared–Visible Image Fusion Method for Defect Detection in Power Transmission Equipment
rows.abstract: Infrared and visible images provide complementary information for transmission equipment inspection, but a single modality is often insufficient to simultaneously represent structural defects and thermal abnormalities. To address this issue, this study proposes a dual-stream thermal-aware infrared–visible image fusion method for transmission equipment defect detection. The method employs separate visible and infrared branches to extract structural texture features and thermal response features, respectively. A shared–specific feature representation and interaction mechanism is then introduced to model visible-specific, infrared-specific, and cross-modal shared information, thereby improving complementary feature integration between the two modalities. In addition, a thermal-aware gated enhancement module adaptively strengthens salient thermal responses while preserving visible structural details. A joint objective consisting of thermal response priority loss, edge preservation loss, and contrast preservation loss is further used to constrain the fusion process. Experiments are conducted on a spatially aligned infrared–visible dataset containing normal insulator strings, normal strain clamps, damaged insulator strings, insulator thermal faults, and strain clamp thermal faults. Comparative results against EgeFusion, DANT-GAN, ITFuse, TDDFusion, and Direct-VI-Fusion demonstrate that the proposed thermal-aware fusion framework achieves improved overall fusion quality and provides more discriminative representations for downstream defect detection. When the fused images are evaluated using a unified YOLO-based detector, the proposed thermal-aware fusion framework achieves precision, recall, and mAP at IoU = 0.5 values of 0.936, 0.921, and 0.943, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed thermal-aware fusion framework can effectively integrate visible structural information and infrared thermal response information and improve the recognition of transmission equipment defects in complex inspection scenarios.

rows.title: Active Collecting and Recirculation of Plasma-Wall Interaction Dust for Programmable Power Exhaust and Long-Term Mantle Stability in Magnetic Confinement Fusion
rows.abstract: The Active Plasma-Wall Interaction Dust Collecting and Controlled Recirculation Mechanism (APWD-HCRM) proposes to collect naturally generated plasma-wall-interaction (PWI) dust and return it to the plasma as a programmable power-exhaust actuator and as material feedstock. We assess the proposal with a pre-registered, replicated design of experiments (DoE): 3.87 million grain trajectories spanning five materials (Li, Be, B, C, W), radii of 0.1–50 µm, six launch locations, launch speeds of 1–1000 m/s, four launch directions and four ion-drag closures, each evaluated over 128 sampled ITER-like edge plasmas. The trajectories are coupled to non-coronal cooling rates, an extended Lengyel model calibrated on neon, an impurity-ion leakage model and a tritium co-deposition budget. Launch location dominates where dust deposits (37.8% of the variance): grains launched from the outer divertor leg or the private-flux dome deposit 39–60% of their mass in the divertor zone with under 1% entering the confined plasma, whereas mid-plane launches ablate within millimetres and deliver nothing to the divertor. Carbon reaches a 78% reduction of divertor heat flux from 1.8×1020 atoms/s (3.5 mg/s); beryllium needs 5.6×1022 atoms/s; lithium stays below 78% up to 1023 atoms/s. In D-T operation, tritium co-deposited with the injected atoms exceeds 1% of the burn rate well below any effective injection rate, so the actuator is confined to non-nuclear phases. A techno-economic assessment of the collection loop closes the paper: recovering tritium from collected dust is the only value stream that clears its processing cost.

rows.title: Adaptive wind power forecasting with multi-level decomposition and multi-branch attention fusion
rows.abstract: Purpose Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for secure and economical power system operation, yet the strong non-stationarity and multiscale fluctuations of wind power signals pose significant challenges to conventional models. Design/methodology/approach This study proposes M2DAF, a hybrid framework that integrates an adaptive multilevel decomposition stage with a multi-branch prediction stage. The decomposition stage employs dynamic complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) with adaptive noise scaling, hierarchical clustering based on morphological features, and variational mode decomposition (VMD) refinement to generate well-separated and physically interpretable components. The prediction stage adopts a parallel convolutional neural network–long short-term memory–Transformer (CNN-LSTM-Transformer) network to capture local, mid-range, and long-range temporal dependencies. An adaptive attention fusion module dynamically adjusts branch contributions at each prediction step. Findings Extensive experiments on three wind farm datasets from France, Turkey, and Spain demonstrate that M2DAF consistently outperforms nine benchmark methods across multiple evaluation metrics. Ablation studies confirm that the decomposition modules contribute most significantly to the overall accuracy. Additional experiments on multi-step forecasting, multivariate inputs, and ramp event prediction under extreme conditions further validate the framework's robustness and cross-regional adaptability across diverse climatic regimes. Overall, the results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed multilevel decomposition and adaptive fusion strategy in capturing the complex, multiscale dynamics of wind power generation. Originality/value This study introduces an adaptive multilevel decomposition and multi-branch attention fusion framework, which innovatively integrates dynamic CEEMDAN, hierarchical clustering, VMD refinement, and a parallel CNN-LSTM-Transformer network with real-time adaptive fusion. This approach effectively addresses the non-stationarity and multiscale nature of wind power data, providing a robust, adaptable solution for highly accurate and reliable wind power forecasting across diverse climatic conditions.

rows.title: An adaptive multiscale hierarchical fusion network for insulator defect detection in UAV power grid inspection
rows.abstract: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based power grid inspection requires robust automated defect recognition for insulators, yet existing detection algorithms struggle with extreme scale variation, complex background clutter, and subtle defect morphology in aerial insulator imagery. This study presents the adaptive multiscale hierarchical fusion network (AMHF-Net), a scenario-oriented detection architecture that builds upon YOLOv8n and introduces targeted adaptations at three architectural levels, each directed at one of these difficulties. The multiscale contextual feature backbone incorporates a Cross Stage Partial Multi-Receptive Field Adaptive Fusion module for parallel multi-granularity feature extraction with channel-adaptive weighting and an Large Separable Kernel Attention-augmented SPPF module for extended contextual perception. The hierarchical multi-level adaptive fusion neck integrates a Pyramid Region-Aware Attention Enhancement module for region-aware spatial dependency modeling, an Selective Gated Fusion module for adaptive gated feature selection, and an Learnable Interpolation Fusion module for detail-preserving learnable interpolation across scales. An Inner-GIoU loss further enhances the precision of bounding box regression. Evaluated on a self-constructed insulator defect dataset, AMHF-Net achieves 51.69% mAP@[0.5:0.95], a gain of 6.76 percentage points over the YOLOv8n baseline while retaining a compact footprint of 3.85 M parameters and 9.7 GFLOPs that is compatible with edge deployment on UAV platforms, and cross-dataset validation on two public benchmarks further verifies its generalization capability. These results confirm that AMHF-Net offers a robust and generalizable approach to automated insulator defect detection in practical UAV-based power grid inspection.

rows.title: Catalyzed deuterium fusion neutron source for the transmutation of minor actinides, production of tritium, and electrical power generation
rows.abstract: The accumulated inventory of spent nuclear fuel in the United States exceeds 90,000 metric tons, with long-term radiological hazards dominated by minor actinides that require isolation for thousands of years. This study details a possible solution to these challenges that also provides significant electrical power. The method employs a fusion system operating in catalyzed deuterium (Cat-D) mode producing the high neutron flux required for this task. It is based on the Compact Field Reversed Configuration Fusion Reactor (CFR2), where the plasma is sequentially compressed to fusion conditions remote from the burn chamber and then translated into the chamber surrounded by the fission blanket. A Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of a subcritical actinide transmutation blanket and the design was optimized. The optimized blanket employs FLiNaK eutectic fluoride salt enriched to 90% 6 Li and containing 17.53 mol% transuranic fluorides as the combined coolant, moderator, and fissile medium. The design achieves keff=0.9695 with a blanket volume of 13.4 m 3 . The FRC is pulsed at 4Hz with a tritium fraction of 4%, yielding a neutron flux of 4×10 18 n/s. This fission system burns 683 kg/yr of TRU, produces 9.6 kg/yr of tritium and 1,431 MWth, requiring only 17.5 MWe to power the CFR2.

rows.title: Cognitive Fusion Questionnaire-Body Image: Psychometric Properties and Its Incremental Power in the Prediction of Binge Eating Severity.
rows.abstract: Given the clinical usefulness of the CFQ-BI (Cognitive Fusion Questionnaire-Body Image; the only existing measure to assess the body-image-related cognitive fusion), the present study aimed to confirm its one-factor structure, to verify its measurement invariance between clinical and non-clinical samples, to analyze its internal consistency and sensitivity to detect differences between samples, as well as to explore the incremental and convergent validities of the CFQ-BI scores in Brazilian samples. This was a cross-sectional study, which was conducted in clinical (women with overweight or obesity in treatment for weight loss) and non-clinical samples (women from the general population). The one-factor structure was confirmed showing factorial measurement invariance across clinical and non-clinical samples. The CFQ-BI scores presented an excellent internal consistency, were able to discriminate clinical and non-clinical samples, and were positively associated with binge eating severity, general cognitive fusion, and psychological inflexibility. Furthermore, body-image-related cognitive fusion scores (CFQ-BI) presented incremental validity over a general measure of cognitive fusion in the prediction of binge eating symptoms. This study demonstrated that CFQ-BI is a short scale with reliable and robust scores in Brazilian samples, presenting incremental and convergent validities, measurement invariance, and sensitivity to detect differences between clinical and non-clinical groups of women, enabling comparative studies between them.

rows.title: Computational modeling of melt pool evolution in laser powder bed fusion with laser power control
Dynamics and Power Balance of Near Unity Target Gain Inertial Confinement Fusion Implosions.
rows.abstract: The change in the power balance, temporal dynamics, emission weighted size, temperature, mass, and areal density of inertially confined fusion plasmas have been quantified for experiments that reach target gains up to 0.72. It is observed that as the target gain rises, increased rates of self-heating initially overcome expansion power losses. This leads to reacting plasmas that reach peak fusion production at later times with increased size, temperature, mass and with lower emission weighted areal densities. Analytic models are consistent with the observations and inferences for how these quantities evolve as the rate of fusion self-heating, fusion yield, and target gain increase. At peak fusion production, it is found that as temperatures and target gains rise, the expansion power loss increases to a near constant ratio of the fusion self-heating power. This is consistent with models that indicate that the expansion losses dominate the dynamics in this regime.

rows.title: Ensemble Entropy with Adaptive Deep Fusion for Short-Term Power Load Forecasting.
rows.abstract: Accurate power load forecasting is crucial for ensuring the safety and economic operation of power systems. However, the complex, non-stationary, and heterogeneous nature of power load data presents significant challenges for traditional prediction methods, particularly in capturing instantaneous dynamics and effectively fusing multi-feature information. This paper proposes a novel framework-Ensemble Entropy with Adaptive Deep Fusion (EEADF)-for short-term multi-feature power load forecasting. The framework introduces an ensemble instantaneous entropy extraction module to compute and fuse multiple entropy types (approximate, sample, and permutation entropies) in real-time within sliding windows, creating a sensitive representation of system states. A task-adaptive hierarchical fusion mechanism is employed to balance computational efficiency and model expressivity. For time-series forecasting tasks with relatively structured patterns, feature concatenation fusion is used that directly combines LSTM sequence features with multimodal entropy features. For complex multimodal understanding tasks requiring nuanced cross-modal interactions, multi-head self-attention fusion is implemented that dynamically weights feature importance based on contextual relevance. A dual-branch deep learning model is constructed that processes both raw sequences (via LSTM) and extracted entropy features (via MLP) in parallel. Extensive experiments on a carefully designed simulated multimodal dataset demonstrate the framework's robustness in recognizing diverse dynamic patterns, achieving MSE of 0.0125, MAE of 0.0794, and R2 of 0.9932. Validation on the real-world ETDataset for power load forecasting confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms baseline models (LSTM, TCN, transformer, and informer) and traditional entropy methods across standard evaluation metrics (MSE, MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2). Ablation studies further verify the critical roles of both the entropy features and the fusion mechanism.

rows.title: Evidential Full-State-Graph-Assisted Fusion for Trustworthy Gas Turbine Power Prediction
Fusion breeding for mid-century, sustainable, carbon free power.
rows.abstract: Fusion has often been billed as the ultimate 21st century sustainable energy source. However, not only is the pace of the program glacially slow, it seems to recede further and further into the future. One way to speed up the delivery of economical fusion could be to change the objective from pure fusion, that is the use of the 14 MeV fusion neutron's kinetic energy to boil water; to fusion breeding, that is the former, but also making use of the neutrons 'potential energy' to breed ten times its energy in the form of nuclear fuel to be burned in separate reactors. The requirements of a fusion breeder are greatly relaxed from the requirements for a pure fusion reactor. For instance, ITER, the large tokamak being built by an international consortium in France, could well be the basis of an economical fusion breeder, but would have to clear many more scientific and technical hurdles before it could become the basis for a pure fusion reactor; hurdles it may or may not be able to clear. Even if it clears them, ITER is unlikely to evolve into an economical pure fusion power supply this century. A fusion breeder as could be alternate approach to speed the delivery of economical of fusion power.

rows.title: Fusion on the Moon:Nuclear Fusion for High-power, Semi-independent Lunar Development
High-power laser powder bed fusion of pure copper for simultaneous achievement of high density and electrical conductivity.
rows.abstract: Pure copper is in high demand for energy and electronic applications due to its superior electrical and thermal conductivities. However, producing dense metals such as copper by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) has long been challenging due to their high infrared reflectivity and thermal conductivity, which can destabilize melting and process stability. In this study, a high-power infrared fiber laser system was employed to characterize the processing parameters, enabling high density and electrical conductivity without post-heat treatment or observable optical degradation during processing. A critical volumetric energy density of approximately 228.76 J mm−3 was identified as the threshold for stable melting, achieved at laser powers ≥ 700 W and scanning speeds ≤ 650 mm s−1. In addition, a linear energy density ≥ 1.0 J mm−1 was required to maintain consistent densification behavior. Under these optimal conditions, the fabricated parts achieved a maximum relative density of 98.9% and an electrical conductivity of up to 100.0% IACS, demonstrating performance comparable to that of wrought copper. Electron backscatter diffraction analysis revealed that electrical conductivity was influenced by both porosity and crystallographic orientation. Specifically, a higher ⟨101⟩ texture fraction and a lower grain-boundary density resulted in reduced electron scattering. These results demonstrate that high-power infrared L-PBF can reliably fabricate pure copper with industrial-level stability in terms of bulk density and conductivity, providing guidelines for the large-scale manufacturing of future electrical and thermal components.

rows.title: High-power short-wavelength Tm-doped fiber amplifier at 1907nm with angle-cleaved fusion splicing.
rows.abstract: An all-fiber high-power short-wavelength Tm-doped fiber (TDF) master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) at 1907nm is presented. The master oscillator is a linear cavity structure that provides a 34.6 W signal light power to the amplifier. In the power amplifier, a method of combining angle-cleaved fusion splicing and gain fiber length cutting has been proved the feasibility for suppressing the parasitic oscillation and improving the output power of the 1907nm laser. By shortening the amplifier gain fiber length to 4 m and fusing the gain fiber at a 5° angle, a maximum output power of 753.1 W at 1907nm with high spectral purity is obtained with a corresponding slope efficiency of 57.7% and optical to optical conversion efficiency of 51.3%. The spatial quality factor and power stability of the TDF MOPA system are 1.60 and 0.1% @ 20 min, respectively. This angle-cleaved fusion splicing method has the potential for mitigating parasitic oscillation in the 1907nm high-power Tm-doped all-fiber MOPA system.

rows.title: Horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion for renewable power forecasting: empirical evidence of a consistent horizon–representation relationship across wind and solar systems
rows.abstract: Accurate renewable power forecasting requires extracting information from both temporal dynamics and frequency-domain fluctuations, yet the optimal balance between these representations across forecasting horizons remains unclear. This study proposes a Horizon-Adaptive Time–Frequency Fusion (HATF) framework that learns horizon-dependent weighting between temporal and spectral features through a lightweight fusion module. Experiments on seven years of operational wind farm SCADA data demonstrate that HATF consistently outperforms recurrent, convolutional, and Transformer-based baselines across forecasting horizons from 15 min to 4 ℎ . Cross-dataset validation on an independent wind turbine dataset and a solar photovoltaic dataset further confirms the robustness of the approach; for the solar dataset, the auxiliary input channels of the model carry irradiance and ambient temperature rather than wind speed and wind direction, preserving the three-channel architecture across energy sources. Ablation studies show that adaptive fusion is essential for effectively integrating time-domain and frequency-domain information. A key finding is that the learned fusion coefficient exhibits a highly consistent approximately linear relationship with forecasting horizon across all datasets ( 𝑅 ⁢ ² > 0 . 9 8 ). Autocorrelation analysis indicates that this behavior is linked to the substantially different persistence timescales of low-frequency and high-frequency signal components, causing the model to gradually shift from frequency-dominant representations at short horizons to time-dominant representations at longer horizons. In addition, a Gaussian prediction head provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates with near-nominal 95% prediction interval coverage. The results suggest that horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion offers both an effective forecasting framework and an interpretable perspective on how predictive information evolves across temporal scales in renewable energy systems.

rows.title: How much laser power can propagate through fusion plasma?
rows.abstract: Propagation of intense laser beams is crucial for inertial confinement fusion, which requires precise beam control to achieve the compression and heating necessary to ignite the fusion reaction. The National Ignition Facility (NIF), where fusion will be attempted, is now under construction. Control of intense beam propagation may be ruined by laser beam self-focusing. We have identified the maximum laser beam power that can propagate through fusion plasma without significant self-focusing and have found excellent agreement with recent experimental data, and suggest a way to increase that maximum by appropriate choice of plasma composition with implication for NIF designs. Our theory also leads to the prediction of anti-correlation between beam spray and backscatter and suggests the indirect control of backscatter through manipulation of plasma ionization state or acoustic damping.

rows.title: Image Fusion and Target Detection Based on Dual ResNet for Power Sensing Equipment.
rows.abstract: Target detection helps to identify, locate, and monitor key components and potential issues in power sensing networks. The fusion of infrared and visible light images can effectively integrate the target the indication characteristics of infrared images and the rich scene detail information of visible light images, thereby enhancing the ability for target detection in power equipment in complex environments. In order to improve the registration accuracy and feature extraction stability of traditional registration algorithms for infrared and visible light images, an image registration method based on an improved SIFT algorithm is proposed. The image is preprocessed to a certain extent, using edge detection algorithms and corner detection algorithms to extract relatively stable feature points, and the feature vectors with excessive gradient values in the normalized visible light image are truncated and normalized again to eliminate the influence of nonlinear lighting. To address the issue of insufficient deep information extraction during image fusion using a single deep learning network, a dual ResNet network is designed to extract deep level feature information from infrared and visible light images, improving the similarity of the fused images. The image fusion technology based on the dual ResNet network was applied to the target detection of sensing insulators in the power sensing network, improving the average accuracy of target detection. The experimental results show that the improved registration algorithm has increased the registration accuracy of each group of images by more than 1%, the structural similarity of image fusion in the dual ResNet network has been improved by about 0.2% compared to in the single ResNet network, and the mean Average Precision (mAP) of the fusion image obtained via the dual ResNet network has been improved by 3% and 6% compared to the infrared and visible light images, respectively.

rows.title: Inertia Estimation for Power Generation Units Based on Dual Neural Networks and a Polynomial Ridge Regression Fusion Model
rows.abstract: In modern power systems, accurate estimation of the inertia of individual generation units is essential for maintaining system stability and identifying weak-inertia areas that require additional inertia support. Conventional neural network ensemble methods based on equal-weight averaging neglect the performance differences among different neural network models. As a result, they cannot fully exploit the complementary strengths of heterogeneous neural network architectures. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an inertia estimation method for power generation units based on dual neural networks and a polynomial ridge regression fusion model. A dual-network framework consisting of a long short-term memory–multilayer perceptron (LSTM–MLP) model and a temporal convolutional network–long short-term memory (TCN–LSTM) model is first constructed. Polynomial ridge regression is then introduced to establish a nonlinear mapping between the inertia estimates produced by the two neural networks and the corresponding true inertia values. This mapping further exploits the complementary capabilities of the two models in time-series feature extraction. The proposed method is validated through comparative, ablation, and noise robustness experiments on the IEEE 14-bus system, and further evaluated on an IEEE 39-bus system containing PV-VSG units. The results demonstrate improved estimation accuracy over the individual models and the equal-weight ensemble, good robustness under Gaussian measurement noise, and relatively high estimation accuracy under different system and generation configurations.

rows.title: Influence of High-Power Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process on the Densification Behavior of AlSi10Mg Alloy
IoT-Enabled Few-Shot Image Generation for Power Scene Defect Detection Based on Self-Attention and Global-Local Fusion.
rows.abstract: Defect detection in power scenarios is a critical task that plays a significant role in ensuring the safety, reliability, and efficiency of power systems. The existing technology requires enhancement in its learning ability from large volumes of data to achieve ideal detection effect results. Power scene data involve privacy and security issues, and there is an imbalance in the number of samples across different defect categories, all of which will affect the performance of defect detection models. With the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), the integration of IoT with machine learning offers a new direction for defect detection in power equipment. Meanwhile, a generative adversarial network based on multi-view fusion and self-attention is proposed for few-shot image generation, named MVSA-GAN. The IoT devices capture real-time data from the power scene, which are then used to train the MVSA-GAN model, enabling it to generate realistic and diverse defect data. The designed self-attention encoder focuses on the relevant features of different parts of the image to capture the contextual information of the input image and improve the authenticity and coherence of the image. A multi-view feature fusion module is proposed to capture the complex structure and texture of the power scene through the selective fusion of global and local features, and improve the authenticity and diversity of generated images. Experiments show that the few-shot image generation method proposed in this paper can generate real and diverse defect data for power scene defects. The proposed method achieved FID and LPIPS scores of 67.87 and 0.179, surpassing SOTA methods, such as FIGR and DAWSON.

rows.title: Leakage-Controlled Multi-View Probability Fusion for DGA-Based Power Transformer Fault Classification: Optimization Ablation and Robustness Analysis
rows.abstract: Dissolved gas analysis is universally used to identify power transformer faults; however, direct neural network optimization can be underpowered when highly correlated gas variables are fed to a small classifier. This study evaluates a leakage-controlled multi-view probability-fusion framework and explicitly tests whether Hybrid Particle Whale Optimization Algorithm (HPWOA) initialization is necessary for the final classifier. The original 595-observation IEC 60599-labelled dataset was audited; six exact predictor duplicates carrying contradictory labels were removed, leaving 589 quality-controlled records. A fixed stratified split produced 471 training and 118 held-out observations. Core15 and Extended34 feature views were modelled with six Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and LightGBM configurations, and five-fold out-of-fold probabilities formed a 36-dimensional input to a six-class softmax fusion layer. In the original optimizer comparison, canonical HPWOA achieved 76.27% held-out accuracy, whereas HPWOA-initialized ten-iteration L-BFGS refinement reached 82.20% accuracy, 82.47% balanced accuracy, 82.51% Macro F1, and 0.9551 Macro-AUC; however, ordinary logistic stacking produced the same held-out correctness pattern. A controlled initialization analysis further showed that the default start and 30 random starts converged to the same hard-label L-BFGS solution, providing no evidence that HPWOA initialization is necessary for the convex fusion layer. The six-model fusion improved held-out accuracy by only 0.84 percentage points over LGBM-Combined49 (81.36%), while adding substantial ensemble and stochastic-search cost. Repeated 5-fold cross-validation over 10 repetitions for the strongest single learner yielded 75.04% ± 4.41% accuracy, and a similarity-grouped leakage stress test yielded 67.39% ± 8.85% accuracy. Held-out accuracy also declined from 87.50% in the nearest train–test similarity stratum to 71.79% in the most dissimilar stratum. These results indicate that the principal contribution lies in leakage-controlled multi-view probability representation and rigorous optimization/robustness ablation rather than an HPWOA-specific predictive advantage. External and transformer-disjoint validation remain necessary before cross-utility generalization can be claimed.

rows.title: Malicious Traffic Detection Method for Power Monitoring Systems Based on Multi-Model Fusion Stacking Ensemble Learning.
rows.abstract: With the rapid development of the internet, the increasing amount of malicious traffic poses a significant challenge to the network security of critical infrastructures, including power monitoring systems. As the core part of the power grid operation, the network security of power monitoring systems directly affects the stability of the power system and the safety of electricity supply. Nowadays, network attacks are complex and diverse, and traditional rule-based detection methods are no longer adequate. With the advancement of machine learning technologies, researchers have introduced them into the field of traffic detection to address this issue. Current malicious traffic detection methods mostly rely on single machine learning models, which face problems such as poor generalization, low detection accuracy, and instability. To solve these issues, this paper proposes a malicious traffic detection method based on multi-model fusion, using the stacking strategy to integrate models. Compared to single models, stacking enhances the model's generalization and stability, improving detection accuracy. Experimental results show that the accuracy of the stacking model on the NSL-KDD test set is 96.5%, with an F1 score of 96.6% and a false-positive rate of 1.8%, demonstrating a significant improvement over single models and validating the advantages of multi-model fusion in malicious traffic detection.

rows.title: MDFNet: a lightweight multi-scale dynamic fusion network for visual measurement of micro-defect in UAV power line inspection
Multi-Source Data Fusion and Virtual Human-Driven Metaverse Digital Twins for Intelligent Power Marketing Service Halls
rows.abstract: To address fragmented business data, limited interaction modalities, substantial demands on manual consultation, and inadequate presentation of low-carbon services in conventional power marketing service halls, this study proposes a human-centered metaverse digital twin framework for power marketing service halls. The framework takes the physical service hall as its operational foundation, uses digital twins to establish a continuously updated correspondence between physical facilities and their virtual representations, and positions digital humans as the primary user-interaction interface. It integrates marketing business systems, cyber-physical system (CPS) energy-management platforms, electricity consumption data collection systems, the State Grid Online platform, RPA process data, and smart home sub-metering data to develop an integrated service environment offering guided tours, business consultation, information visualization, service recommendations, and carbon-footprint displays. In addition, the proposed architecture encompasses a heterogeneous data-fusion model, a mechanism for generating digital-human service scripts, a method for constructing metaverse scenes, and a carbon-footprint assessment component. Together, these elements support a closed-loop workflow extending from the interpretation of customer requests to business responses, scene interaction, and feedback-informed service refinement. The reported evaluation indicates shorter service-completion times, improved question-answering accuracy and confidence calibration, more favorable assessments of immersion and interaction, and stronger capabilities for displaying marketing information and communicating low-carbon energy services. These results are reported outcomes of the study and require confirmation against the underlying evaluation data.

rows.title: NEXUS-PLASMA CIVIL POWER: Direct Fusion-Driven Plasma-MHD Power Generation & Thermal Recovery
rows.abstract: Version 6.2 presents a conceptual civil power research architecture with D-T fusion as the primary proposed source and separately accounted neutron/thermal and charged-particle/plasma pathways. It treats coupling to magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) conversion as an unresolved physical interface requiring transport modeling, conservation checks, and independent specialist review. The dossier provides governing relations, explicit channel and system energy boundaries, a recalculable numerical illustration, measurement and uncertainty requirements, and Go/No-Go validation gates. Phase I is a non-nuclear surrogate study using a calibrated electrical/RF plasma source. No operating fusion reactor, experimentally demonstrated direct fusion-to-MHD coupling, or net-positive system power is claimed. Includes a mathematical and engineering illustrated annex. English, fusion-primary illustrated international evaluation edition dated 29 September 2026.

Power from Fusion
Rank-Based Distribution Reshaping for Robust EM/Power Fusion in Side-Channel Analysis Across Sampling Rates

Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Method Based on Fusion of Cloud Map Features and Historical-Power Data.
rows.abstract: Existing data-fusion-driven photovoltaic (PV) power-forecasting methods do not fully exploit cloud-image information. Simple feature concatenation cannot explicitly describe high-order interactions between cloud imagery and historical power, whereas full high-order fusion tensors introduce substantial parameter and computational overhead. This paper proposes a short-term PV power-forecasting method that fuses ground-based cloud-image features with historical-power data. MAGAN is used to enhance the brightness and texture representation of ground-based cloud images. An improved CNN-Transformer with a multi-scale separable convolution (MSC) module extracts multi-scale spatial cloud features. Low-rank tensor fusion (LTF) models cross-modal interactions between cloud-image and power features under a low-rank constraint and the fused sequence is fed into an improved Pyraformer with an i-Pyra module to forecast four 15 min steps over the next hour. Experiments using 2021 measurements from a 100 kW PV station in Jiangxi Province show that MAGAN-enhanced cloud images reach a PSNR of 7.25 dB and an SSIM of 0.75. On the independent test set, the proposed method obtains MAE, MAPE, and RMSE values of 21.8%, 17.6%, and 32.4%, respectively, reducing the three errors by 13.1%, 15.8%, and 15.2% compared with a cloud-feature and sample-weighted Pyraformer, while reducing fusion-layer parameters by 46.7% relative to full bilinear fusion.

rows.title: Spatial prior and defect co-occurrence constraint fusion for vibration damper defect detection in power lines
rows.abstract: Abstract In UAV-based power line inspection, vibration dampers occupy only a tiny fraction of pixels and are surrounded by cluttered backgrounds, leading to under-utilized spatial priors, high false-positive localization errors, and severe category confusion. To address these challenges, we present a novel framework, termed PGMD-Net, which integrates spatial layout priors and defect co-occurrence constraints to systematically infuse domain knowledge into fine-grained object detection. First, the Spatial Prior Aware Hybrid Extraction Module (SPA-HEM) translates physical power line layout rules into deterministic spatial heatmaps that explicitly highlight damper-probable regions. Second, the Hybrid Attention Fusion Localization (HAF-Loc) module employs an attention-gated mechanism to merge these geometric priors with data-driven convolutional features, effectively injecting the physical constraints of damper distributions into the network hypothesis space to achieve prior-driven, precise target localization. Finally, the Co-occurrence Adjacency Graph Classification (CoAG-Cls) module leverages an empirical defect co-occurrence matrix to initialize a prior-weighted adjacency matrix, performing relation-aware graph convolutions to propagate inter-defect semantic relational constraints for robust fine-grained recognition. Extensive experiments on our self-constructed UAV dataset demonstrate that PGMD-Net attains 86.9% precision, 83.9% recall, 89.0% mAP@0.5, and 61.4% mAP@[0.5:0.95], achieving competitive performance against existing object detection methods and confirming the effectiveness of physical knowledge injection for complex industrial defect detection tasks.

rows.title: Spatio-temporal PV power forecasting considering the time-shift correction and the information fusion strategy of multi-stations.
rows.abstract: Accurate prediction of PV power is essential to ensuring the safe and economic operation of power systems with high PV penetration. The current PV power prediction scheme considering the spatio-temporal correlation characteristics is relatively simple in data processing, resulting in low prediction accuracy; at the same time, the missing data also poses a great problem to the prediction. Therefore, in order to improve the prediction accuracy and solve the problem of missing data, this paper proposes a PV power spatio-temporal prediction model considering time-shift correction and a multi-station information fusion strategy Firstly, relevant power station clusters are constructed using hierarchical clustering, and a similar daily data filtering model considering the variation characteristics of daily power characteristic curves is proposed to filter the data; Secondly, multiple BP neural network models are constructed and multiple reference power stations with high relevance are predicted using irradiance information; Thirdly, the prediction results of multiple reference power stations are input to the data processing module for time-shift analysis and spatial correlation information fusion correction, which solves the missing data problem of the target power station to be predicted. Finally, it is input to One-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network(1DCNN) to achieve the power prediction of the target power station with missing data. The simulation analysis shows that the root mean square error (RMSE) of a sunny day forecast is 3.31%; the RMSE of a non-sunny day forecast is 9.65%, which proves the accuracy of this two-layer neural network is higher compared to other model structures, so the proposed scheme has certain reliability and accuracy in the prediction of PV power with missing data.

rows.title: Study of parametrized plasma response and regime for consistent stopping power models of α particles in D-T and p-11 B fusion scenarios
rows.abstract: Abstract This work develops a systematic parameterization of plasma response regimes in deuterium–tritium ($D$-$T$) and proton–boron ($p$–$^{11}$B) fusion plasmas using a set of dimensionless plasma parameters. These parameters describe the thermodynamic state of the plasma, its collective response properties, as well as the kinetic properties of energetic fusion-born alpha particles in terms of dimensionless ratios of characteristic velocities, collision/oscillation frequencies, and relevant interaction length scales. Special emphasis is put on $\alpha$-electron and $\alpha$-ion interaction metrics, which define the main energy-loss channels. By determining these dimensionless parameters across representative fusion-relevant density-temperature domains, the numerical analysis identifies the plasma regime controlling alpha-particle transport in ($D$-$T$) and ($p$–$^{11}$B) plasmas. The results show that, under typical conditions for inertial confinement fusion, the plasmas are weakly to moderately coupled, weakly perturbed, and in a weakly non-degenerate regime, implying a consistent physical description where the energy exchange is governed by the collective response of the plasma. This study allows the identification of the operational domains in which reduced-stopping-power descriptions, such as the binary collision or dielectric response approaches, remain physically justifiable and numerically stable. This allows for the development of a physics-based framework in which to validate reduced transport models without the need for kinetic or quantum-level complexities. The parameterization aims at facilitating the integration of validated stopping models into advanced particle simulation toolboxes that include Monte Carlo approaches, such as GEANT4, for more valid virtual experiments in the study of fusion plasmas.

rows.title: The Thermodynamic and Financial Reality of AI Power Starvation: Rider's Bremsstrahlung Limit in Pulsed D-3He Fusion, Tokamak REBCO Supply-Chain Scaling, PJM/FERC Queue Bottlenecks, and Hyperscale Stranded-CapEx Risk
rows.abstract: By 2026, generative artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure expansion has collided with hard physical and grid-regulatory walls. International Energy Agency (IEA) projections indicate global data center electricity consumption surging from 460 TWh (2024) to > 1,000 TWh by 2030 (~320 Mt CO2/yr) and 1,300 TWh by 2035—exceeding Japan's entire national electricity demand—while single campuses such as Microsoft's Fairwater facility (3.3 GW) and the $500 billion Stargate initiative (10 GW) strain regional transmission limits amid a projected $740 billion global 2026 AI capital expenditure (CapEx) cycle. To assuage investor and ESG anxieties, hyperscalers have promoted a narrative of imminent baseload salvation via commercial nuclear fusion (Helion Energy, Commonwealth Fusion Systems [CFS]) and Generation-IV Small Modular Reactors (SMRs; Kairos Power). Building upon our prior CERN Zenodo monographs on the CMOS CapEx cliff and Willow quantum transition (Record 23353509), 1.8 fJ/spike room-temperature neuromorphic quantum computing (Record 23334854), and Delaware Caremark fiduciary governance (Record 23360530), this monograph conducts a rigorous plasma-physical, grid-regulatory, and balance-sheet audit of Big Tech's next-generation nuclear and fusion scenarios. We establish four core findings: (1) Rider's Bremsstrahlung Limit & Inductive Recovery Infeasibility in Pulsed D-3He FRC: While Helion Energy secured Washington DOH RML/RAEL licenses in June 2026 for its Orion plant under a 50 MW (2028) PPA with Microsoft, D-3He ignition at T_i ≈ 50 keV suffers catastrophic Bremsstrahlung losses (P_Brem > P_fus in thermal equilibrium). Sustaining T_i >> T_e against rapid Spitzer Coulomb equilibration forces ultra-short pulses requiring an engineeringly implausible magnetic energy recovery efficiency η_rec in [0.999, 0.9999], alongside unmitigated 2.45 MeV D-D side-reaction neutrons and tritium; (2) Tokamak REBCO Supply Chains vs. Gen-IV SMR Pragmatism: CFS's 20 T SPARC/ARC tokamak (paired with DeepMind RL magnetic sweeping and TORAX) and Google's 500 MW Kairos Power FHR-TRISO PPA (accelerated by the 2024 ADVANCE Act and April 2026 NRC 10 CFR Part 53 licensing) represent scientifically grounded 2030s pathways, yet face acute first-of-a-kind (FOAK) cost inflation exemplified by NuScale's $9.3 billion (> $20,000/kW) cancellation; (3) LBNL Queue Paralysis, PJM Capacity Explosion, and FERC Co-Location Vetoes: With 2,061 GW trapped in 61-month U.S. interconnection queues (13% completion rate), PJM capacity prices spiking 833% to $269.92/MW-day (and hitting the $333.44 cap for 2027/2028 with a 6,623 MW shortfall), and FERC rejecting AWS/Talen's Susquehanna nuclear co-location expansion, hyperscalers are forced onto 116 GW backlogged GE Vernova gas turbines, $110-$115/MWh Three Mile Island restarts, and $210-$292/MWh tariff-inflated LFP BESS; and (4) The Stranded-CapEx Impairment Theorem: Because GPU economic half-lives (τ_1/2 ≈ 1 yr) are an order of magnitude shorter than power delivery lead times (τ_power in [5, 15] yr), unenergized CMOS CapEx faces catastrophic balance-sheet write-downs (98.0% impairment at median 5.08-year queue lag) unless replaced by room-temperature quantum-phononic architectures.
