rows.title: 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) Memristive In-Sensor Computing and Neuromorphic Vision Chips: Atomically Thin Photodetectors, Sub-Nanosecond Optoelectronic Modulation, and Edge Visual Processing
rows.abstract: Autonomous vision systems, edge artificial intelligence, and real-time robotics are fundamentally constrained by the energy-prohibitive data transfer overhead between separated image sensors (CMOS cameras) and digital processing units (GPUs, TPUs). In-Sensor Computing establishes a transformative paradigm shift that fuses optical sensing, non-volatile memory, and neural computation directly into a single unified atomically thin hardware layer. TwoDimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (2D TMDs, such as MoS2, WSe2, and MoSe2) provide an exceptional material platform for optoelectronic in-sensor computing, featuring direct bandgaps, high optical absorption coefficients, pronounced excitonic effects, and memristive conductance switching via trap-assisted charge-trapping. By integrating 2D TMD photodetectors with memristive crossbar arrays, artificial vision chips can capture visual inputs, store synaptic weights, and execute parallel matrix-vector multiplications for feature extraction and pattern recognition natively at the optical focal plane with sub-nanosecond latency and ultra-low power dissipation. However, translating atomically thin TMD optoelectronic devices from laboratory flakes into wafer-scale in-sensor vision chips introduces profound physical and manufacturing bottlenecks: high contact resistance at metal-TMD interfaces, spatial variations in defect density causing conductance drift, sub-bandgap trap relaxation kinetics limiting frame rates, and large-scale 2D material growth uniformity. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of 2D TMD memristive in-sensor computing and neuromorphic vision chips. We formalize optoelectronic photoconductive gain via trap-assisted recombination models, derive crossbar in-sensor dot-product transfer functions, and model spatiotemporal spiking vision processing. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise multi-physics co-simulation and physical wafer-scale testbed evaluating 64x64 MoS2 optoelectronic memristive crossbar arrays across real-time edge image classification (MNIST, CIFAR-10) and optical pattern recognition. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our 2D MoS2 in-sensor vision chip achieves an energy efficiency of 342.4 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W)—a 35x improvement over conventional CMOS camera-GPU pipelines—while sustaining a sub-nanosecond sensing-computation latency and 97.8% image classification accuracy. Finally, we formulate open challenges in wafer-scale 2D epitaxy, multispectral color filtering, and all-optical reset mechanisms.

rows.title: 3D Point Cloud Object Detection on Edge Devices for Split Computing
rows.abstract: The field of autonomous driving technology is rapidly advancing, with deep learning being a key component. Particularly in the field of sensing, 3D point cloud data collected by LiDAR is utilized to run deep neural network models for 3D object detection. However, these state-of-the-art models are complex, leading to longer processing times and increased power consumption on edge devices. The objective of this study is to address these issues by leveraging Split Computing, a distributed machine learning inference method. Split Computing aims to lessen the computational burden on edge devices, thereby reducing processing time and power consumption. Furthermore, it minimizes the risk of data breaches by only transmitting intermediate data from the deep neural network model. Experimental results show that splitting after voxelization reduces the inference time by 70.8% and the edge device execution time by 90.0%. When splitting within the network, the inference time is reduced by up to 57.1%, and the edge device execution time is reduced by up to 69.5%.

rows.title: 5G Converged Network Resource Allocation Strategy Based on Reinforcement Learning in Edge Cloud Computing Environment.
rows.abstract: Aiming at the problem that computing power and resources of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) servers are difficult to process long-period intensive task data, this study proposes a 5G converged network resource allocation strategy based on reinforcement learning in edge cloud computing environment. n order to solve the problem of insufficient local computing power, the proposed strategy offloads some tasks to the edge of network. Firstly, we build a multi-MEC server and multi-user mobile edge system, and design optimization objectives to minimize the average response time of system tasks and total energy consumption. Then, task offloading and resource allocation process is modeled as Markov decision process. Furthermore, the deep Q-network is used to find the optimal resource allocation scheme. Finally, the proposed strategy is analyzed experimentally based on TensorFlow learning framework. Experimental results show that when the number of users is 110, final energy consumption is about 2500 J, which effectively reduces task delay and improves the utilization of resources.

rows.title: A Survey of Security in Cloud, Edge, and Fog Computing.
rows.abstract: The field of information security and privacy is currently attracting a lot of research interest. Simultaneously, different computing paradigms from Cloud computing to Edge computing are already forming a unique ecosystem with different architectures, storage, and processing capabilities. The heterogeneity of this ecosystem comes with certain limitations, particularly security and privacy challenges. This systematic literature review aims to identify similarities, differences, main attacks, and countermeasures in the various paradigms mentioned. The main determining outcome points out the essential security and privacy threats. The presented results also outline important similarities and differences in Cloud, Edge, and Fog computing paradigms. Finally, the work identified that the heterogeneity of such an ecosystem does have issues and poses a great setback in the deployment of security and privacy mechanisms to counter security attacks and privacy leakages. Different deployment techniques were found in the review studies as ways to mitigate and enhance security and privacy shortcomings.

rows.title: Accelerator Virtualization in Fog Computing: Moving From the Cloud to the Edge
rows.abstract: Hardware accelerators are available on the Cloud for enhanced analytics. Next generation Clouds aim to bring enhanced analytics using accelerators closer to user devices at the edge of the network for improving Quality-of-Service by minimizing end-to-end latencies and response times. The collective computing model that utilizes resources at the Cloud-Edge continuum in a multi-tier hierarchy comprising the Cloud, the Edge and user devices is referred to as Fog computing. This article identifies challenges and opportunities in making accelerators accessible at the Edge. A holistic view of the Fog architecture is key to pursuing meaningful research in this area.

rows.title: Characterizing Application Scheduling on Edge, Fog and Cloud Computing Resources
rows.abstract: Cloud computing has grown to become a popular distributed computing service offered by commercial providers. More recently, Edge and Fog computing resources have emerged on the wide-area network as part of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. These three resource abstraction layers are complementary, and provide distinctive benefits. Scheduling applications on clouds has been an active area of research, with workflow and dataflow models serving as a flexible abstraction to specify applications for execution. However, the application programming and scheduling models for edge and fog are still maturing, and can benefit from learnings on cloud resources. At the same time, there is also value in using these resources cohesively for application execution. In this article, we present a taxonomy of concepts essential for specifying and solving the problem of scheduling applications on edge, for and cloud computing resources. We first characterize the resource capabilities and limitations of these infrastructure, and design a taxonomy of application models, Quality of Service (QoS) constraints and goals, and scheduling techniques, based on a literature review. We also tabulate key research prototypes and papers using this taxonomy. This survey benefits developers and researchers on these distributed resources in designing and categorizing their applications, selecting the relevant computing abstraction(s), and developing or selecting the appropriate scheduling algorithm. It also highlights gaps in literature where open problems remain.

rows.title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics
rows.abstract: Mobility analytics using data generated from the Internet of Mobile Things (IoMT) is facing many challenges which range from the ingestion of data streams coming from a vast number of fog nodes and IoMT devices to avoiding overflowing the cloud with useless massive data streams that can trigger bottlenecks [1]. Managing data flow is becoming an important part of the IoMT because it will dictate in which platform analytical tasks should run in the future. Data flows are usually a sequence of out-of-order tuples with a high data input rate, and mobility analytics requires a real-time flow of data in both directions, from the edge to the cloud, and vice-versa. Before pulling the data streams to the cloud, edge data stream processing is needed for detecting missing, broken, and duplicated tuples in addition to recognize tuples whose arrival time is out of order. Analytical tasks such as data filtering, data cleaning and low-level data contextualization can be executed at the edge of a network. In contrast, more complex analytical tasks such as graph processing can be deployed in the cloud, and the results of ad-hoc queries and streaming graph analytics can be pushed to the edge as needed by a user application. Graphs are efficient representations used in mobility analytics because they unify knowledge about connectivity, proximity and interaction among moving things. This poster describes the preliminary results from our experimental prototype developed for supporting transit systems, in which edge and cloud computing are combined to process transit data streams forwarded from fog nodes into a cloud. The motivation of this research is to understand how to perform meaningfulness mobility analytics on transit feeds by combining cloud and fog computing architectures in order to improve fleet management, mass transit and remote asset monitoring

rows.title: Design and experimental analysis of a cloud-edge collaborative computing resource scheduling algorithm integrating deep reinforcement learning
rows.abstract: It includes the design and performance evaluation of algorithms to address challenges of computing resource scheduling in cloud-edge collaborative environment including great heterogeneity, high dynamism and concurrent constraints. A cloud-edge collaborative system model is built and reinforcement learning mechanisms are used to model the scheduling process. The three mechanisms are: state perception, action decision making and feedback of reward to gain adaptive resource allocation. To evaluate the algorithm performance in a few aspects such as task latency, energy consumption and load balancing, simulation experiments are carried out. The results show that this approach is effective in decreasing task completion latency and system energy consumption under different loads, and also increasing the efficiency of resource utilization, which has excellent stability and adaptability.

rows.title: Edge AI for Energy-Efficient Smart IoT Systems: A Sustainable Computing Approach
rows.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) is transforming Internet of Things (IoT) systems by enabling data-driven decisions close to the point where data are generated. However, conventional cloud-centric architectures can introduce communication overhead, latency, privacy concerns, and additional energy costs. This paper examines Edge AI as a sustainable computing approach for energy-efficient smart IoT systems, with particular relevance to the development priorities associated with Viksit Bharat 2047. The study follows a descriptive and analytical approach based on research literature concerning TinyML, on-device machine learning, Edge AI, and energy-aware IoT. It proposes an architecture consisting of sensing, local inference, edge coordination, selective cloud processing, and energy-aware orchestration. The paper further identifies measurable parameters including accuracy, inference latency, energy per inference, communication volume, memory footprint, and reliability for evaluating sustainable AIoT systems. The objective is not to claim unverified experimental results, but to establish a practical research framework that can subsequently be tested on resource-constrained edge hardware. The study indicates that sustainable AIoT should be evaluated not only through predictive performance but also through the computational, communication, and energy resources required to deliver each intelligent decision.

rows.title: Edge and Cloud Computing in Smart Cities
rows.abstract: The evolution of smart cities is intrinsically linked to advancements in computing paradigms that support real-time data processing, intelligent decision-making, and efficient resource utilization. Edge and cloud computing have emerged as fundamental pillars that enable scalable, distributed, and latency-aware services in urban environments. Cloud computing provides extensive computational capabilities and centralized data storage, whereas edge computing ensures localized processing to mitigate network congestion and latency. This survey presents an in-depth analysis of the integration of edge and cloud computing in smart cities, highlighting architectural frameworks, enabling technologies, application domains, and key research challenges. The study examines resource allocation strategies, real-time analytics, and security considerations, emphasizing the synergies and trade-offs between cloud and edge computing paradigms. The present survey also notes future directions that address critical challenges, paving the way for sustainable and intelligent urban development.

rows.title: Edge, Fog, and Cloud Against Disease: The Potential of High-Performance Cloud Computing for Pharma Drug Discovery.
rows.abstract: The high-performance computing (HPC) platform for large-scale drug discovery simulation demands significant investment in speciality hardware, maintenance, resource management, and running costs. The rapid growth in computing hardware has made it possible to provide cost-effective, robust, secure, and scalable alternatives to the on-premise (on-prem) HPC via Cloud, Fog, and Edge computing. It has enabled recent state-of-the-art machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools for drug discovery, such as BERT, BARD, AlphaFold2, and GPT. This chapter attempts to overview types of software architectures for developing scientific software or application with deployment agnostic (on-prem to cloud and hybrid) use cases. Furthermore, the chapter aims to outline how the innovation is disrupting the orthodox mindset of monolithic software running on on-prem HPC and provide the paradigm shift landscape to microservices driven application programming (API) and message parsing interface (MPI)-based scientific computing across the distributed, high-available infrastructure. This is coupled with agile DevOps, and good coding practices, low code and no-code application development frameworks for cost-efficient, secure, automated, and robust scientific application life cycle management.

rows.title: Edge-Fog-Cloud Computing Hierarchy for Improving Performance and Security of NB-IoT-Based Health Monitoring Systems.
rows.abstract: This paper proposes a three-computing-layer architecture consisting of Edge, Fog, and Cloud for remote health vital signs monitoring. The novelty of this architecture is in using the Narrow-Band IoT (NB-IoT) for communicating with a large number of devices and covering large areas with minimum power consumption. Additionally, the architecture reduces the communication delay as the edge layer serves the health terminal devices with initial decisions and prioritizes data transmission for minimizing congestion on base stations. The paper also investigates different authentication protocols for improving security while maintaining low computation and transmission time. For data analysis, different machine learning algorithms, such as decision tree, support vector machines, and logistic regression, are used on the three layers. The proposed architecture is evaluated using CloudSim, iFogSim, and ns3-NB-IoT on real data consisting of medical vital signs. The results show that the proposed architecture reduces the NB-IoT delay by 59.9%, the execution time by an average of 38.5%, and authentication time by 35.1% for a large number of devices. This paper concludes that the NB-IoT combined with edge, fog, and cloud computing can support efficient remote health monitoring for large devices and large areas.

rows.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
rows.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

rows.title: Fog computing and its role in the internet of things
rows.abstract: Fog Computing extends the Cloud Computing paradigm to the edge of the network, thus enabling a new breed of applications and services. Defining characteristics of the Fog are: a) Low latency and location awareness; b) Wide-spread geographical distribution; c) Mobility; d) Very large number of nodes, e) Predominant role of wireless access, f) Strong presence of streaming and real time applications, g) Heterogeneity. In this paper we argue that the above characteristics make the Fog the appropriate platform for a number of critical Internet of Things (IoT) services and applications, namely, Connected Vehicle, Smart Grid, Smart Cities, and, in general, Wireless Sensors and Actuators Networks (WSANs).

rows.title: Neuromorphic Computing Architectures for Low-Power Edge Inference in IoT Applications
rows.abstract: The blistering advancements witnessed in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem have led to the urgency of search outcomes that provide energy efficient, low latency, and smart processing support that manifests itself right at the edge. The traditional edge computing devices built on von Neumann architecture are inherently limited by being optimized to be adjacent in memory and processing components, which results in the high power required and latency, which are highly undesirable in devices with limited power resources; wearables, smart sensors, and remote-monitoring systems. A Neuromorphic computing approach based on the human brain blueprint presents a better alternative due to its implementation of spiking neural networks (SNNs) that allow asynchronous and event-driven computation, thus dramatically lowering power demand and yet being able to run real-time inference. This paper includes a holistic comparison of the most recent examples of the neuromorphic hardware platforms, such as Intel Loihi, IBM TrueNorth, and BrainScaleS system, with regard to their learning architectures, energy consumption, throughput, and suitability to the edge-based IoT applications. An empirical case study is carried out, which is a keyword spotting case study and event-based gesture recognition case study using Google Speech Commands and the DVS Gesture dataset sets, respectively. The neuromorphic systems presented a significant energy per inference improvement up to 15x and reduced latency at about 30 on traditional ARM Cortex-M7-based ANN implementations at very slight sacrifices in terms of classification accuracy. In addition, the Loihi platform showed on-chip learning utilizing spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), which made the platform capable of dynamic and adaptive inference in fluctuating IoT applications. This paper also examines the integration issues of neuromorphic systems which include the compatibility with sensor modalities, immature software toolchains, and complexities to convert ANN to SNN. The results indicate that neuromorphic systems are highly suitable in ultra-low-power edge intelligence and provide a paradigm of scalable and biologically inspired, next-generation IoT systems. The lines of future research are described in such aspects as hybrid neuromorphic edge-cloud learning, unification of benchmark requirements, and designing secure, programmable, and reconfigurable neuromorphic co-processors to support adaptive edge AI.

rows.title: Neuromorphic Spin-Torque Nano-Oscillators and Coupled Magnonic Networks: Nonlinear Dynamics, Frequency Entrainment, and Edge Reservoir Computing
rows.abstract: Edge artificial intelligence, real-time wireless classification, and high-frequency time-series forecasting demand hardware architectures capable of processing complex temporal dynamics at ultra-low power levels without conventional digital clock bottlenecks. Spin-Torque Nano-Oscillators (STNOs) establish an exceptional nanoscale spintronic hardware platform that generates microwave-frequency oscillatory signals through direct spin-transfer torque excitation of magnetization precession. By coupling multiple STNOs into interacting magnonic networks, these non-linear nano-oscillators emulate biological spiking neurons and dynamical reservoirs, enabling high-speed edge reservoir computing and pattern recognition natively in the spintronic domain. However, translating STNO arrays from physical device physics into production neuromorphic accelerators introduces severe physical and manufacturing bottlenecks: strong thermal phase noise jitter broadening spectral linewidths, weak mutual coupling strengths restricting synchronization topologies, inhomogeneous fabrication variations across nanoscale pillars, and complex non-linear frequency entrainment. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of neuromorphic spin-torque nano-oscillators and coupled magnonic networks. We formalize magnetization dynamics via the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski (LLGS) equation with STT active damping modulation, derive Adler equations for mutual phase synchronization and frequency entrainment, and model spin-wave bus propagation. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SPICE and hardware-in-the-loop testbed evaluating 64-node STNO neuromorphic arrays across spoken digit recognition and real-time wireless anomaly detection. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our synchronized magnonic network achieves a 97.4% classification accuracy on spoken digit recognition while operating at gigahertz frequencies within an ultra-low power envelope of 42 nanowatts per oscillator—outperforming digital recurrent neural networks by over three orders of magnitude in energy efficiency. Finally, we formulate open challenges in thermal noise suppression, all-magnonic transistorless logic, and scalable 3D magnetic interconnect integration.

rows.title: Optimizing storage on fog computing edge servers: A recent algorithm design with minimal interference.
rows.abstract: The burgeoning field of fog computing introduces a transformative computing paradigm with extensive applications across diverse sectors. At the heart of this paradigm lies the pivotal role of edge servers, which are entrusted with critical computing and storage functions. The optimization of these servers' storage capacities emerges as a crucial factor in augmenting the efficacy of fog computing infrastructures. This paper presents a novel storage optimization algorithm, dubbed LIRU (Low Interference Recently Used), which synthesizes the strengths of the LIRS (Low Interference Recency Set) and LRU (Least Recently Used) replacement algorithms. Set against the backdrop of constrained storage resources, this research endeavours to formulate an algorithm that optimizes storage space utilization, elevates data access efficiency, and diminishes access latencies. The investigation initiates a comprehensive analysis of the storage resources available on edge servers, pinpointing the essential considerations for optimization algorithms: storage resource utilization and data access frequency. The study then constructs an optimization model that harmonizes data frequency with cache capacity, employing optimization theory to discern the optimal solution for storage maximization. Subsequent experimental validations of the LIRU algorithm underscore its superiority over conventional replacement algorithms, showcasing significant improvements in storage utilization, data access efficiency, and reduced access delays. Notably, the LIRU algorithm registers a 5% increment in one-hop hit ratio relative to the LFU algorithm, a 66% enhancement over the LRU algorithm, and a 14% elevation in system hit ratio against the LRU algorithm. Moreover, it curtails the average system response time by 2.4% and 16.5% compared to the LRU and LFU algorithms, respectively, particularly in scenarios involving large cache sizes. This research not only sheds light on the intricacies of edge server storage optimization but also significantly propels the performance and efficiency of the broader fog computing ecosystem. Through these insights, the study contributes a valuable framework for enhancing data management strategies within fog computing architectures, marking a noteworthy advancement in the field.

rows.title: PRICE: Privacy-Preserving Image Classification in Mobile Edge-Cloud Computing with Homomorphic Encryption
rows.abstract: Cloud-assisted image classification enables many mobile AI applications, but transmitting raw images to the cloud raises significant privacy concerns. Homomorphic encryption (HE) allows computation over encrypted data; however, existing end-to-end HE-based inference pipelines incur prohibitive latency and computational overhead, limiting their feasibility for latency-sensitive mobile systems. This paper addresses how to enable efficient encrypted image classification in mobile edge-cloud environments without sacrificing accuracy. We propose PRICE, a three-tier edge-cloud architecture that partitions deep neural network inference between a trusted edge and an untrusted cloud. The edge performs lightweight feature extraction in plaintext, while only compact embeddings are encrypted using the Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) scheme and offloaded to the cloud for encrypted final-layer inference. This design avoids homomorphic evaluation of deep backbone layers, significantly reducing computation depth, ciphertext size, and end-to-end latency. To further improve efficiency, we develop RowHyDiag, a row-packed hybrid diagonal encoding with hoisted-rotation-aware encrypted matrix-vector computation, which minimizes rotation operations and improves slot utilization. Extensive experiments on real devices across five datasets demonstrate that, under the evaluated 128-bit-security configurations, RowHyDiag achieves up to 31.8$\times$ faster cloud inference, 85.3$\times$ fewer rotations, and 83.0$\times$ lower setup payload than the conventional Halevi-Shoup diagonal method. RowHyDiag also outperforms the PEGASUS linear-transformation baseline, providing 1.1-4.5$\times$ faster cloud inference and 1.2-3.4$\times$ lower setup payload. The results show that PRICE enables deployment-ready, low-latency encrypted inference for mobile edge-cloud systems under a trusted-edge threat model.

rows.title: Process migration-based computational offloading framework for IoT-supported mobile edge/cloud computing
rows.abstract: Mobile devices have become an indispensable component of Internet of Things (IoT). However, these devices have resource constraints in processing capabilities, battery power, and storage space, thus hindering the execution of computation-intensive applications that often require broad bandwidth, stringent response time, long battery life, and heavy computing power. Mobile cloud computing and mobile edge computing (MEC) are emerging technologies that can meet the aforementioned requirements using offloading algorithms. In this paper, we analyze the effect of platform-dependent native applications on computational offloading in edge networks and propose a lightweight process migration-based computational offloading framework. The proposed framework does not require application binaries at edge servers and thus seamlessly migrates native applications. The proposed framework is evaluated using an experimental testbed. Numerical results reveal that the proposed framework saves almost 44% of the execution time and 84% of the energy consumption. Hence, the proposed framework shows profound potential for resource-intensive IoT application processing in MEC.

rows.title: Securing real-time traffic analytics with a privacy-preserving edge and cloud computing framework
rows.abstract: The recent demand for real-time traffic management in urban environments has led to the adoption of edge and cloud computing, which improve the efficiency, scalability, and security of traffic analytics. Nevertheless, the privacy and confidentiality of traffic data remain important issues. In this study, a privacy-sensitive real-time traffic analytics system is proposed that combines edge computing for local-area data processing and cloud computing for large-scale analytics. This system uses blockchain, encryption, and differential privacy to safeguard sensitive traffic information and ensure information integrity and confidentiality. The proposed system was evaluated through a set of simulation experiments and compared with existing models, namely BFRT, FedTSE, FLAGCN, and VehiCast. The results indicate that the suggested system is more successful at reducing latency, power consumption, and load balancing, and at improving data security, achieving 30% latency reduction and 15-30% power reduction. In addition, the system was highly scalable, able to process an increasing number of edge devices and cloud servers without significant performance impairment. The work overall offers a scalable, robust real-time traffic control platform and insight into integrating the edge-cloud computing system into intelligent transportation systems (ITS) with privacy-preserving technologies.

rows.title: SimTune: bridging the simulator reality gap for resource management in edge-cloud computing.
rows.abstract: Industries and services are undergoing an Internet of Things centric transformation globally, giving rise to an explosion of multi-modal data generated each second. This, with the requirement of low-latency result delivery, has led to the ubiquitous adoption of edge and cloud computing paradigms. Edge computing follows the data gravity principle, wherein the computational devices move closer to the end-users to minimize data transfer and communication times. However, large-scale computation has exacerbated the problem of efficient resource management in hybrid edge-cloud platforms. In this regard, data-driven models such as deep neural networks (DNNs) have gained popularity to give rise to the notion of edge intelligence. However, DNNs face significant problems of data saturation when fed volatile data. Data saturation is when providing more data does not translate to improvements in performance. To address this issue, prior work has leveraged coupled simulators that, akin to digital twins, generate out-of-distribution training data alleviating the data-saturation problem. However, simulators face the reality-gap problem, which is the inaccuracy in the emulation of real computational infrastructure due to the abstractions in such simulators. To combat this, we develop a framework, SimTune, that tackles this challenge by leveraging a low-fidelity surrogate model of the high-fidelity simulator to update the parameters of the latter, so to increase the simulation accuracy. This further helps co-simulated methods to generalize to edge-cloud configurations for which human encoded parameters are not known apriori. Experiments comparing SimTune against state-of-the-art data-driven resource management solutions on a real edge-cloud platform demonstrate that simulator tuning can improve quality of service metrics such as energy consumption and response time by up to 14.7% and 7.6% respectively.

rows.title: THE EL-RAKHAWI HYBRID PHOTONIC-IONIC POWER UNIT FOR EDGE AI COMPUTING
rows.abstract: The El-Rakhawi Hybrid Photonic-Ionic Power Unit for Edge AI Computing (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23508399) addresses critical energy bottlenecks in decentralized AI deployment by eliminating dependence on lithium-based batteries and grid infrastructure. This PCT-ready patent specification discloses an integrated architecture combining perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells achieving 30%+ efficiency under AM1.5G conditions with sodium-ion battery storage substantially free of lithium components. The system's core innovation is a direct DC coupling architecture comprising a DC-DC converter that eliminates intermediate AC-DC conversion stages, providing a low-noise, fast-transient power profile with ripple voltage <50 mV specifically matching photonic neural network accelerator requirements. The sodium-ion battery employs layered transition metal oxide cathode (Na_x Fe_y Mn_z O_2) with hard carbon anode, achieving 95%+ round-trip efficiency under specified charge/discharge rates. Validated across three deployment scenarios (rural medical diagnostics, oceanic monitoring, lunar habitat simulation), the system delivers 72-120 hours continuous operation with LCOE of $0.08-0.12/kWh, 40-60% lower than lithium-based alternatives. Comprehensive IP protection covers 15 claims spanning system, method, solar cell, and battery architectures. All moral, financial, and proprietary rights exclusively reserved to Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi—establishing a commercially viable pathway for sustainable, autonomous edge AI computing worldwide.

rows.title: Advanced Therapies for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Critical Review of Gene-, RNA-, and Cell-Based Strategies to Address Residual Risk
rows.abstract: Background. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) can progress despite contemporary kidney-protective treatment, motivating the development of additional mechanism-based interventions. This critical narrative review evaluates whether gene-, RNA-, and cell-based strategies are ready to address this residual risk and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. Methods. A targeted literature verification and update was undertaken for the revision, with emphasis on primary intervention studies, contradictory findings, and the distinction between target validation and product efficacy. Mechanistic and model system background is considered in relation to therapeutic selection. Results. Adeno-associated viral vectors offer potentially durable expression but face species-dependent renal tropism, immunity, and limited control after administration. RNA therapeutics permit time-limited modulation, although productive renal delivery and compartment-specific effects remain unresolved. Mesenchymal stromal cells and extracellular vesicles provide broader paracrine activity, with challenges in potency definition, biodistribution, and manufacturing. Autologous renal cell products have entered clinical testing but require individualized production and invasive delivery. Most gene and RNA evidence is preclinical; cell therapy trials provide feasibility or exploratory efficacy signals rather than definitive kidney protection. Conclusions. Thus, at present, progress toward routine DKD use requires reproducible renal target engagement, validated manufacturing, and confirmation of clinical benefit in randomized trials.

rows.title: AMYGDALIN AS A POTENTIAL THERAPY FOR BREAST CANCER VIA BAX/BCL2 GENE-MEDIATED APOPTOSIS
rows.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) remains one of the most common and difficult-to-treat malignant diseases in global public health, requiring the development of more selective and less toxic therapeutic approaches. In this context, natural compounds have gained increasing attention due to their biological potential in regulating tumor cell processes. Amygdalin (C20H27NO11), a natural cyanogenic glycoside found in the seeds of plants from the Rosaceae family and often referred to as “vitamin B17”, has been studied for its possible anticancer effects. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of amygdalin on the expression of apoptosis-related genes and on cell viability in two human BC cell lines with different molecular profiles: MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7. The cells were treated with amygdalin at a concentration of 50 mg/mL for 24 hours, while NHDF (Normal Human Dermal Fibroblast) cells (Sigma Aldrich) were used as the control group. The expression levels of the pro-apoptotic gene BAX and the anti apoptotic gene BCL-2 were assessed using RT-qPCR, while cell viability was analyzed using standard cytotoxicity methods. The results showed a cell-specific gene expression modulation. In MDA-MB-231 cells, amygdalin treatment led to an increase in the expression of both BAX and BCL-2 genes. In MCF-7 cells, a decrease in the expression of both genes was observed, together with a significant reduction in cell viability. These findings suggest that amygdalin has different biological effects depending on the cellular context and tumor molecular profile, thus supporting its potential role in modulating apoptotic pathways in BC cells and pointing towards the amygdalin therapeutic applicability.

rows.title: Exploring the Endeavors of CRISPR/Cas9 Gene-Editing Technology in the Therapy of Cancer and Other Human Diseases
rows.abstract: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and the associated Cas9 nuclease have become the dominant platform for genome editing, offering greater efficiency, simplicity and programmability than the zinc finger nucleases and transcription activator-like effector nucleases that preceded them. This review examines the application of CRISPR/Cas9 to cancer and to other human diseases, together with the obstacles that continue to limit its clinical translation. We outline the architecture and DNA-recognition mechanisms of the three programmable nuclease platforms, describe the classification of CRISPR/Cas systems into two classes and their constituent types, and summarise the pooled genome-wide screening formats knock-out, interference and activation libraries through which the technology has been used to identify essential genes, synthetic-lethal interactions and mechanisms of drug resistance. In cancer research, CRISPR/Cas9 has enabled the inactivation of tumour suppressor genes in animal models, the restoration of tumour suppressor function, and the dissection of resistance to targeted agents and cytotoxic chemotherapy. Its most advanced clinical application is in cell therapy, where multiplexed editing has been used to disrupt the endogenous T cell receptor, silence checkpoint genes such as PDCD1 and reduce the risk of graft-versus-host disease; early-phase trials in refractory malignancy have established feasibility and an acceptable safety profile, although objective responses have so far been limited. Beyond oncology, progress is reviewed in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, HIV-1 infection, sickle cell disease, haemophilia B and neurodevelopmental disorders. Off-target cleavage, delivery and vector immunogenicity remain the principal constraints on therapeutic use, and the strategies developed to address them are discussed.

rows.title: Integrated Dual-Gene (OTOF & GJB2) Regenerative Therapy, Thermo-Responsive Hydrogel Matrix, and Micro-Infusion Delivery System for Complete Hearing Loss Restoration Across All Age Groups
rows.abstract: वैज्ञानिक शोध लेख (Research Article) शीर्षक: OTOF एवं GJB2 जीन थेरेपी, हाइड्रोजेल कैरियर और माइक्रो-इन्फ्यूजन डिलीवरी प्रणाली द्वारा जन्मजात एवं उम्र-संबंधित बहरेपन का पूर्ण निवारण: एक एकीकृत न्यूरो-रिजेनरेटिव मॉडल मुख्य आविष्कारकर्ता (Principal Inventor): बंटी कुमावत क्षेत्र: जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी (Biotechnology), जीन थेरेपी (Gene Therapy), पुनर्योजी चिकित्सा (Regenerative Medicine) १. प्रस्तावना (Introduction) मानव कान के आंतरिक हिस्से (Cochlea) में स्थित श्रवण कोशिकाएं (Hair Cells) नष्ट होने के बाद प्राकृतिक रूप से दोबारा नहीं बनती हैं। विश्व स्तर पर बहरेपन का सबसे बड़ा कारण GJB2 (Connexin 26 प्रोटीन की कमी) और OTOF (Otoferlin प्रोटीन की कमी) जीन्स में म्यूटेशन होना है। वर्तमान चिकित्सा विज्ञान में इन दोनों समस्याओं का एक साथ और हर उम्र के लिए कोई स्थायी इलाज उपलब्ध नहीं है। आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा विकसित यह तकनीक एक ऐसा अनूठा फॉर्मूला और डिलीवरी सिस्टम प्रस्तुत करती है, जो न केवल आनुवंशिक कमियों को सुधारता है, बल्कि कान की मृत कोशिकाओं का पुनर्जन्म (Regeneration) करके मस्तिष्क के श्रवण केंद्रों को दोबारा सक्रिय करता है। २. मुख्य फॉर्मूला और प्रयोगशाला निर्माण (The Molecular Formula) इस आविष्कार का मुख्य आधार एक जैविक मिश्रण (Biological Cocktail) है जिसे प्रयोगशाला में अत्यंत सुरक्षित वातावरण में तैयार किया जाता है: • जीन संयोजन: इस फॉर्मूले में GJB2 और OTOF जीन्स की 100% स्वस्थ और शुद्ध प्रतियों (Healthy Copies) को आपस में जोड़ा गया है। • हानिरहित लिक्विड वेक्टर: इन जीन्स को कान की कोशिकाओं के केंद्रक तक सुरक्षित पहुँचाने के लिए एक विशेष हानिरहित लिक्विड वेक्टर (जैसे Adeno-Associated Virus या AAV) में मिश्रित किया गया है। यह लिक्विड बिना किसी संक्रमण के जीन को स्थानांतरित करने का माध्यम बनता है। ३. स्मार्ट डिलीवरी मैकेनिज्म (The Surgical Delivery System) दवा को कान के सबसे संवेदनशील भीतरी हिस्से (Cochlea) तक बिना किसी नुकसान के पहुँचाने के लिए तीन आधुनिक तकनीकों को एकीकृत किया गया है: 1. High-Powered Surgical Microscope: यह डॉक्टर को कान के भीतरी पर्दे (Round Window Membrane) का सटीक और बड़ा त्रिविमीय (3D) दृश्य प्रदान करता है। 2. Micro-Infusion Pump: कान के भीतरी तरल पर दबाव (Fluid Pressure) को रोकने के लिए, यह पंप बेहद धीमी गति (0.1 माइक्रोलीटर प्रति सेकंड) से दवा को इंजेक्ट करता है, जिससे कान की नसें सुरक्षित रहती हैं। 3. बायो-कंपैटिबल हाइड्रोजेल (Hydrogel): दवा को इस विशेष जेल के साथ मिलाया जाता है। कान के अंदरूनी तापमान (37°C) पर पहुँचते ही यह लिक्विड से जेली जैसा गाढ़ा हो जाता है। इससे दवा सुई के छेद से बाहर नहीं बहती और धीरे-धीरे (Sustained Release) कोशिकाओं द्वारा सोख ली जाती है। ४. इलाज की श्रृंखला और सुरक्षा स्विच (Set of Series & Shut-off Switch) यह थेरेपी किसी भी उम्र के मरीज पर काम कर सके, इसके लिए इसे एक श्रृंखला (Series) के रूप में डिज़ाइन किया गया है: • २४ दिनों का कमीशन प्रोटोकॉल: यह इलाज एक ही बार में भारी मात्रा में देने के बजाय २४ दिनों के अंतराल की एक श्रृंखला (Set of Series) में दिया जाता है। इससे कोशिकाओं को धीरे-धीरे विकसित होने का समय मिलता है और उम्र का बंधन खत्म हो जाता है। • मॉलिक्यूलर शट-ऑफ स्विच (Maru Set of Switch): कोशिकाओं के पुनर्जन्म की प्रक्रिया को नियंत्रित करने के लिए फॉर्मूले में एक जेनेटिक टाइमर या रासायनिक स्विच (जैसे Tet-On/Off) जोड़ा गया है। जैसे ही कान के अंदर आवश्यक मात्रा में नई कोशिकाओं का निर्माण पूरा हो जाता है, यह स्विच दवा के असर को स्वचालित रूप से बंद (OFF) कर देता है, जिससे ट्यूमर या ओवरग्रोथ का खतरा शून्य हो जाता है। ५. मस्तिष्क का सक्रिय होना और परिणाम (Neurological Activation) दवा के कान में इंजेक्ट होने के बाद की कार्यप्रणाली को दो स्तरों पर देखा जा सकता है: • कान का सुधार (Peripheral Repair): फॉर्मूला कान की खराब कोशिकाओं को हटाकर स्वस्थ जीन स्थापित करता है और निष्क्रिय कोशिकाओं को नई सुनने वाली कोशिकाओं में बदल देता है। • दिमाग का सक्रिय होना (Central Activation): जैसे ही कान से इलेक्ट्रिकल सिग्नल निकलने शुरू होते हैं, वे श्रवण तंत्रिका के माध्यम से सीधे मस्तिष्क तक पहुँचते हैं। इससे दिमाग के दो मुख्य हिस्से सक्रिय होते हैं: 1. Auditory Cortex (ऑडिटरी कॉर्टेक्स): जो आवाज को साफ-साफ सुनने और समझने की क्षमता को वापस लाता है। 2. Broca's Area (ब्रोका का क्षेत्र): जो व्यक्ति को सुनने के साथ-साथ साफ और सही तरीके से बोलने में मदद करता है। ६. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत का यह एकीकृत मॉडल (Integrated Model) जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग और सर्जिकल रोबोटिक्स का एक अद्भुत संगम है। यह दुनिया का पहला ऐसा दावा है जो उम्र की सीमा को समाप्त करके बहरेपन का एक अचूक, सुरक्षित और तार्किक निवारण प्रदान करता है। वैज्ञानिक शोध लेख (Research Article) - अपडेटेड संस्करण शीर्षक: OTOF एवं GJB2 जीन थेरेपी, हाइड्रोजेल कैरियर और माइक्रो-इन्फ्यूजन डिलीवरी प्रणाली द्वारा जन्मजात एवं उम्र-संबंधित बहरेपन का पूर्ण निवारण: एक एकीकृत न्यूरो-रिजेनरेटिव मॉडल मुख्य आविष्कारकर्ता (Principal Inventor): बंटी कुमावत क्षेत्र: जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी (Biotechnology), जीन थेरेपी (Gene Therapy), पुनर्योजी चिकित्सा (Regenerative Medicine) १. प्रस्तावना (Introduction) मानव कान के आंतरिक हिस्से (Cochlea) में स्थित श्रवण कोशिकाएं (Hair Cells) नष्ट होने के बाद प्राकृतिक रूप से दोबारा नहीं बनती हैं। विश्व स्तर पर बहरेपन का सबसे बड़ा कारण GJB2 (Connexin 26 प्रोटीन की कमी) और OTOF (Otoferlin प्रोटीन की कमी) जीन्स में म्यूटेशन होना है। वर्तमान चिकित्सा विज्ञान में इन दोनों समस्याओं का एक साथ और हर उम्र के लिए कोई स्थायी इलाज उपलब्ध नहीं है। आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा विकसित यह तकनीक एक ऐसा अनूठा फॉर्मूला और डिलीवरी सिस्टम प्रस्तुत करती है, जो न केवल आनुवंशिक कमियों को सुधारता है, बल्कि कान की मृत कोशिकाओं का पुनर्जन्म (Regeneration) करके मस्तिष्क के श्रवण केंद्रों को दोबारा सक्रिय करता है। २. दवा निर्माण की चरणबद्ध प्रयोगशाला विधि (Method of Manufacturing & Formula) इस शक्तिशाली जैव-रासायनिक मिश्रण (Biochemical Cocktail) को प्रयोगशाला में PC2/BSL-2 (Bio-Safety Level 2) के अत्यंत सुरक्षित और रोगाणुहीन (Sterile) वातावरण में निम्नलिखित चार चरणों में तैयार किया जाता है: चरण ए: स्वस्थ जीन्स का पृथक्करण और क्लोनिंग (Gene Cloning) 1. GJB2 और OTOF का चयन: सबसे पहले प्रयोगशाला में डीएनए सिंथेसाइज़र (DNA Synthesizer) की मदद से मानव के स्वस्थ GJB2 और OTOF जीन्स का न्यूक्लियोटाइड अनुक्रम (Sequence) तैयार किया जाता है। 2. आकार का प्रबंधन (Dual-Vector Split): चूँकि OTOF जीन का आकार बड़ा (लगभग 6 kb) होता है, इसलिए इसे दो भागों (Front half और Back half) में विभाजित किया जाता है, ताकि यह वायरस वेक्टर में आसानी से फिट हो सके। GJB2 जीन को उसके सामान्य रूप में रखा जाता है। चरण बी: वायरल वेक्टर (वाहन) का निर्माण (Vector Packaging) 1. हानिरहित वायरस का चयन: इस फॉर्मूले के लिए Adeno-Associated Virus Serotype 9 (AAV9) या AAV-anc80 का चयन किया जाता है, जो कान की भीतरी नसों के लिए पूरी तरह सुरक्षित और हानिरहित (Harmless) होते हैं। 2. जेनेटिक कोडिंग: इन वायरस के हानिकारक हिस्से (Replication genes) को निकालकर बाहर कर दिया जाता है। उनकी जगह पर हमारे तैयार किए गए स्वस्थ GJB2 और OTOF जीन्स को "प्रमोटर" (Promoter - जैसे CMV या CAG प्रमोटर, जो जीन को चालू रखता है) के साथ जोड़कर वायरस के खोल (Capsid) के अंदर पैक कर दिया जाता है। चरण सी: मॉलिक्यूलर शट-ऑफ स्विच जोड़ना (Integrating the Maru Switch) 1. इसी जेनेटिक कोडिंग के दौरान, जीन के साथ Tet-On (Tetracycline-Inducible) सिस्टम का डीएनए कोड जोड़ा जाता है। 2. यह कोड दवा के अंदर एक 'आणविक बटन' की तरह काम करता है, जो केवल तभी सक्रिय होगा जब शरीर में एक निश्चित उत्प्रेरक (जैसे Doxycycline) मौजूद हो। चरण डी: अंतिम तरल मिश्रण तैयार करना (Final Liquid Formulation) 1. शुद्धिकरण (Purification): तैयार वेक्टर्स को अल्ट्रासेंट्रीफ्यूजेशन (Ultracentrifugation) तकनीक द्वारा पूरी तरह शुद्ध किया जाता है ताकि कोई अवांछित तत्व न बचे। 2. कंसंट्रेशन (Viral Titer): इस साफ किए गए लिक्विड को एक बफर सॉल्यूशन (जैसे Phosphate-Buffered Saline) में मिलाया जाता है। इसका गाढ़ापन (Titer) 1 × 10¹² viral genomes/mL निर्धारित किया जाता है ताकि बहुत कम मात्रा में भी अरबों स्वस्थ जीन मौजूद रहें। 3. हाइड्रोजेल मिश्रण: अंतिम चरण में, इस तैयार लिक्विड दवा को उपयोग से ठीक पहले थर्मो-रिस्पॉन्सिव हाइड्रोजेल (जैसे Poloxamer 407) के साथ 1:1 के अनुपात में मिलाया जाता है। यह जेल कमरे के तापमान पर लिक्विड रहता है लेकिन कान के अंदर जाते ही सेमी-सॉलिड (जेली) बन जाता है। ३. स्मार्ट डिलीवरी मैकेनिज्म (The Surgical Delivery System) दवा को कान के सबसे संवेदनशील भीतरी हिस्से (Cochlea) तक बिना किसी नुकसान के पहुँचाने के लिए तीन आधुनिक तकनीकों को एकीकृत किया गया है: 1. High-Powered Surgical Microscope: यह डॉक्टर को कान के भीतरी पर्दे (Round Window Membrane) का सटीक और बड़ा त्रिविमीय (3D) दृश्य प्रदान करता है। 2. Micro-Infusion Pump: कान के भीतरी तरल पर दबाव (Fluid Pressure) को रोकने के लिए, यह पंप बेहद धीमी गति (0.1 माइक्रोलीटर प्रति सेकंड) से सुई के जरिए केवल ५ से १० माइक्रोलीटर दवा को इंजेक्ट करता है। 3. हाइड्रोजेल का कार्य: कान के अंदरूनी तापमान (37°C) पर पहुँचते ही जेल दवा को बाहर बहने से रोकता है और उसे धीरे-धीरे रिलीज करता है। ४. इलाज की श्रृंखला (Set of Series) यह थेरेपी किसी भी उम्र के मरीज पर काम कर सके, इसके लिए इसे एक श्रृंखला (Series) के रूप में डिज़ाइन किया गया है: • २४ दिनों का कमीशन प्रोटोकॉल: यह इलाज एक ही बार में भारी मात्रा में देने के बजाय २४ दिनों के अंतराल की एक श्रृंखला (Set of Series) में दिया जाता है। इससे कोशिकाओं को धीरे-धीरे विकसित होने का समय मिलता है और उम्र का बंधन खत्म हो जाता है। काम पूरा होते ही 'मारू शट-ऑफ स्विच' दवा के असर को स्वचालित रूप से बंद (OFF) कर देता है। ५. मस्तिष्क का सक्रिय होना और परिणाम (Neurological Activation) • कान का सुधार (Peripheral Repair): फॉर्मूला कान की खराब कोशिकाओं को हटाकर स्वस्थ जीन स्थापित करता है और निष्क्रिय सहायक कोशिकाओं (Supporting Cells) को बिल्कुल नई सुनने वाली कोशिकाओं (Hair Cells) में बदल देता है। • दिमाग का सक्रिय होना (Central Activation): जैसे ही कान से इलेक्ट्रिकल सिग्नल निकलने शुरू होते हैं, वे सीधे मस्तिष्क तक पहुँचते हैं जिससे Auditory Cortex (आवाज पहचानने वाला हिस्सा) और Broca's Area (बोलने की क्षमता वाला हिस्सा) पूरी तरह एक्टिव हो जाते हैं। मरीज न केवल सुन पाता है बल्कि साफ तरीके से बोलना भी सीख जाता है। ६. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत का यह एकीकृत मॉडल (Integrated Model) जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग और सर्जिकल रोबोटिक्स का एक अद्भुत संगम है। यह दुनिया का पहला ऐसा दावा है जो उम्र की सीमा को समाप्त करके बहरेपन का एक अचूक, सुरक्षित और तार्किक निवारण प्रदान करता है। वैज्ञानिक शोध लेख (Research Article) शीर्षक: OTOF एवं GJB2 जीन थेरेपी, हाइड्रोजेल कैरियर और माइक्रो-इन्फ्यू

rows.title: NTAP NF1 Gene Replacement Initiative- Development of a gene replacement therapy for cutaneous neurofibromas related to NF1
Pediatric Alexander Disease: Clinical Spectrum, GFAP Genotype–Phenotype Relationships, Molecular Pathogenesis, and Emerging Gene-Targeted Therapies
rows.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare, dominantly inherited astrocytopathy caused principally by heterozygous pathogenic variants in GFAP, the gene encoding glial fibrillary acidic protein. In children, the disorder spans a continuum from neonatal or early-infantile encephalopathy with severe cerebral white-matter disease, seizures, hydrocephalus and rapid developmental compromise to later childhood phenotypes with mixed cerebral, bulbar, pyramidal and autonomic involvement. The historical age-based categories of infantile, juvenile and adult disease are therefore increasingly complemented by clinically and radiologically grounded cerebral, intermediate and bulbospinal phenotypes. This critical narrative review integrates clinical natural-history data, magnetic resonance imaging patterns, GFAP genotype–phenotype evidence, mechanistic studies in human tissue, induced pluripotent stem cell models and animal models, and the translational development of GFAP-lowering therapies. Evidence published from January 2001 to 8 August 2026 was prioritised, with older foundational observations considered when necessary. The strongest mechanistic evidence supports a toxic gain-of-function model in which mutant GFAP misassembly and pathological accumulation amplify GFAP transcription, disturb proteostasis, activate stress and inflammatory pathways, alter astrocytic morphology and homeostatic functions, and secondarily impair neurons, oligodendrocytes and myelination. Genotype is informative but not deterministic: recurrent variants at residues such as Arg79 and Arg239 show meaningful differences in age at onset and survival, yet substantial within-variant variability limits individual prognostication. Fluid GFAP is a biologically direct target-engagement biomarker, but its value as an independent clinical outcome biomarker is constrained when GFAP itself is therapeutically suppressed. Antisense oligonucleotide-mediated GFAP reduction has reversed major pathological features in preclinical models and has progressed to a late-stage intrathecal clinical programme. The field is consequently shifting from diagnosis and supportive care towards mechanism-based intervention, but paediatric trial design still requires age-sensitive functional outcomes, validated surrogate markers, genotype-aware stratification and longer-term assessment of developmental trajectories and treatment safety.

rows.title: Permanent Cure for Periodic Paralysis: A Mathematical and Scientific Model for Nano-Immuno Evasive CRISPR Gene Replacement Therapy
rows.abstract: पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस का स्थायी समाधान: नैनो-क्रिसप्र और इम्यून-इवेसिव जीन थेरेपी आविष्कारकर्ता (Concept Developer): बंटी कुमावत विषय: जेनेटिक मेडिसिन और नैनो-बायोटेक्नोलॉजी प्रस्तावना (Introduction) पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस (Periodic Paralysis) एक अत्यंत जटिल अनुवांशिक (Genetic) बीमारी है, जिसमें मरीजों को समय-समय पर मांसपेशियों में गंभीर कमजोरी और पैरालिसिस के दौरों का सामना करना पड़ता है। वर्तमान चिकित्सा पद्धति में इस बीमारी को केवल दवाओं (जैसे Acetazolamide) और खान-पान के संतुलन से नियंत्रित किया जाता है, लेकिन इसका कोई स्थायी इलाज उपलब्ध नहीं है। आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत ने इस बीमारी को जड़ से खत्म करने के लिए एक अभूतपूर्व वैज्ञानिक मॉडल प्रस्तावित किया है, जो नैनो टेक्नोलॉजी (Nanotechnology), उन्नत जीन एडिटिंग (CRISPR), और सुरक्षित वायरल वेक्टर्स (Engineered AAV) के अनूठे संगम पर आधारित है। मूल सिद्धांत और कार्यप्रणाली (The Core Scientific Model) बंटी कुमावत का यह मॉडल मुख्य रूप से तीन क्रांतिकारी चरणों में काम करता है: 1. इम्यून सिस्टम को 'धोखा' देना और सुरक्षित वायरस का चुनाव (Immune Evasion via Capsid Engineering) पारंपरिक जीन थेरेपी में सबसे बड़ी बाधा यह होती है कि हमारा इम्यून सिस्टम (रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता) दवा ले जाने वाले वायरस को दुश्मन मानकर नष्ट कर देता है। इस मॉडल के तहत, मांसपेशियों के लिए सबसे सटीक माने जाने वाले AAV9 (Adeno-Associated Virus 9) या MyoAAV वायरस का चयन किया जाएगा। इस वायरस के बाहरी आवरण (Capsid) पर नैनो टेक्नोलॉजी की मदद से एक विशेष 'केमिकल कोडिंग' (Stealth Polymer Coating) की जाएगी। यह कोडिंग शरीर के इम्यून सिस्टम के लिए एक 'अदृश्य सुरक्षा कवच' की तरह काम करेगी। इसके परिणामस्वरूप, इम्यून सिस्टम इस वायरस को बाहरी खतरा न समझकर शरीर का ही एक हिस्सा मानेगा और इसे सुरक्षित रूप से खून के जरिए पूरे शरीर में फैलने देगा। 2. नैनो-टार्गेटिंग: सीधे मांसपेशियों तक पहुँच (Targeted Muscle Delivery) यह तकनीक सुनिश्चित करती है कि दवा शरीर के अन्य अंगों (जैसे लीवर या किडनी) में जाकर कोई साइड-इफेक्ट न पैदा करे। वायरस के ऊपर लगाए गए नैनो-कण (Nanoparticles) केवल कंकाल मांसपेशियों (Skeletal Muscle Cells) की सतह पर मौजूद विशिष्ट रिसीवर्स को पहचानेंगे। यह 'लॉक और की' (Lock and Key) सिस्टम की तरह काम करेगा, जिससे यह थेरेपी सीधे मांसपेशियों के कणों और कोशिकाओं के भीतर प्रवेश कर जाएगी। 3. खराब जीन को डिलीट करना और नया फिट करना (Knockdown and Replace via CRISPR) कोशिका के केंद्रक (Nucleus) में पहुँचने के बाद, यह सिस्टम पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस के लिए जिम्मेदार मुख्य खराब जीनों को लक्षित करेगा: • CACNA1S (कैल्शियम चैनल) • SCN4A (सोडियम चैनल) • KCNJ2 (पोटेशियम चैनल) यहाँ CRISPR-Cas9 तकनीक एक जेनेटिक कैंची की तरह काम करेगी। यह इन जीनों के उत्परिवर्तित (Mutated) या खराब हिस्से को ढूंढकर वहां से हमेशा के लिए डिलीट (Cut) कर देगी। इसके तुरंत बाद, नैनो-कैरियर द्वारा साथ लाया गया बिल्कुल स्वस्थ और नया जीन उस खाली जगह पर पूरी सटीकता के साथ फिट कर दिया जाएगा। भविष्य का परिणाम (The Ultimate Outcome) जब मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं में यह जेनेटिक सुधार (Genetic Correction) पूरा हो जाएगा, तो शरीर में पूरी तरह से स्वस्थ और सामान्य आयन चैनल्स (Ion Channels) का निर्माण होने लगेगा। इसके बाद पोटेशियम, सोडियम या कैल्शियम का उतार-चढ़ाव मांसपेशियों को प्रभावित नहीं कर पाएगा और मरीज को पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस के दौरों से हमेशा के लिए मुक्ति मिल जाएगी। निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) बंटी कुमावत द्वारा यह "नैनो-क्रिसप्र और इम्यून-इवेसिव जीन रिप्लेसमेंट मॉडल" भविष्य की चिकित्सा विज्ञान का एक सटीक ब्लूप्रिंट है। यदि इस सैद्धांतिक मॉडल को अत्याधुनिक प्रयोगशालाओं में परीक्षण (Clinical Trials) के जरिए अमली जामा पहनाया जाए, तो यह अनुवांशिक बीमारियों के इतिहास में एक मील का पत्थर साबित हो सकता है। शोध पत्र और निर्माण मार्गदर्शिका (Research Paper & Manufacturing Guide) परियोजना का नाम: नैनो-इम्यूनो इवेसिव जीन थेरेपी (Myo-Stealth Vaccine) मुख्य आविष्कारकर्ता: बंटी कुमावत उद्देश्य: पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस (CACNA1S, SCN4A, KCNJ2 जनित) का पूर्ण और स्थायी उन्मूलन। भाग 1: वैज्ञानिक लेख (Scientific Article) प्रस्तावना (Introduction) पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस एक ऐसी गंभीर आनुवंशिक बीमारी है जो मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं की झिल्ली (Cell Membrane) पर मौजूद आयन चैनलों को बाधित करती है। आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा प्रस्तावित यह मॉडल पारंपरिक वैक्सीन की तरह केवल संक्रमण से नहीं लड़ता, बल्कि शरीर के भीतर जाकर डिफेक्टिव जेनेटिक कोड को री-राइट (पुनर्लेखन) करता है। इसे "मायो-स्टेल्थ जीन थेरेपी वैक्सीन" कहा जा सकता है। यह तकनीक नैनो-इंजीनियरिंग, इम्यूनो-अल्टरेशन और उन्नत CRISPR-Cas9 का एक आदर्श संयोजन है। कार्य सिद्धांत (Mechanism of Action) यह थेरेपी मुख्यतः तीन स्तंभों पर टिकी है: 1. प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली से सुरक्षा (Immune Shielding): शरीर का डिफेंस सिस्टम बाहरी डिलीवरी एजेंटों को नष्ट न कर सके, इसके लिए एक छद्म आवरण (Stealth Coating) का उपयोग। 2. ऊतक-विशिष्ट लक्ष्यीकरण (Tissue-Specific Targeting): पूरे शरीर में दवा को व्यर्थ गंवाने के बजाय केवल कंकाल मांसपेशियों (Skeletal Muscles) को लक्षित करना। 3. आनुवंशिक सुधार (Genetic Restoration): खराब जीन को हटाकर स्वस्थ डीएनए को स्थायी रूप से स्थापित करना। भाग 2: वैक्सीन निर्माण की चरण-दर-चरण विधि (Step-by-Step Manufacturing Methodology) नोट: यह प्रक्रिया अत्याधुनिक जैव-सुरक्षा स्तर-3 (BSL-3) प्रयोगशालाओं और जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग उपकरणों के माध्यम से संपन्न की जाती है। [चरण 1: जेनेटिक असेंबली] ➔ [चरण 2: वायरल वेक्टर उत्पादन] ➔ [चरण 3: नैनो-कैप्सिड कोडिंग] ➔ [चरण 4: गुणवत्ता जांच] चरण 1: जेनेटिक पेलोड की तैयारी (Designing the CRISPR & Healthy Gene Construct) सबसे पहले कंप्यूटर सॉफ़्टवेयर (Bioinformatics Tools) की मदद से लक्षित जेनेटिक पेलोड का खाका तैयार किया जाता है। • अंग १ (गाइड RNA - gRNA): एक विशिष्ट आरएनए अनुक्रम तैयार किया जाता है जो मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं के भीतर जाकर CACNA1S, SCN4A, या KCNJ2 के ठीक उसी हिस्से से जुड़ता है जहाँ म्यूटेशन (खराबी) है। • अंग २ (Cas9 एंजाइम): आणविक कैंची (Molecular Scissors) का डीएनए कोड जो खराब हिस्से को काटेगा। • अंग ३ (स्वस्थ डोनर डीएनए): प्रयोगशाला में कृत्रिम रूप से संश्लेषित (Synthesized) इन तीनों जीनों का बिल्कुल स्वस्थ और त्रुटिहीन डीएनए अनुक्रम। चरण 2: सही वायरल वेक्टर (MyoAAV) का उत्पादन दवा को कोशिका के अंदर तक ले जाने के लिए एक हानिरहित और कुशल वाहक की आवश्यकता होती है। • कोशिका संवर्धन (Cell Culture): प्रयोगशाला में HEK293 (ह्यूमन एम्ब्रियोनिक किडनी) कोशिकाओं को संवर्धित किया जाता है। • ट्रांसफेक्शन (Transfection): इन कोशिकाओं के भीतर MyoAAV या AAV9 प्लास्मिड डीएनए डाला जाता है। यह वायरस प्राकृतिक रूप से मांसपेशियों के प्रति अत्यधिक आकर्षण रखता है। • पेलोड पैकेजिंग: वायरस के गुणन के दौरान, चरण 1 में तैयार किया गया CRISPR पेलोड और स्वस्थ डीएनए इस वायरस के खोखले केंद्र (Capsid) के भीतर पैक हो जाता है। चरण 3: नैनो-टेक्नोलॉजी द्वारा कैप्सिड कोडिंग (Stealth Nano-Coating) वायरस तैयार होने के बाद, इसे इम्यून सिस्टम से बचाने के लिए बंटी कुमावत के फॉर्मूले के अनुसार नैनो-इंजीनियरिंग की जाती है। • पॉलीमर कॉन्जुगेशन (PEGylation): वायरस के बाहरी प्रोटीन आवरण पर पॉलीइथाइलीन ग्लाइकोल (PEG) या विशिष्ट लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल्स (LNPs) का एक नैनो-आवरण चढ़ाया जाता है। • परिणाम: यह नैनो-कोडिंग वायरस के उन हिस्सों को छुपा देती है जिन्हें देखकर हमारी प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली (Antibodies) हमला करती हैं। अब यह वायरस शरीर के लिए 'अदृश्य' (Stealth) हो जाता है। • टार्गेटिंग लिगैंड्स: इस नैनो-परत के ऊपर विशेष पेप्टाइड्स लगाए जाते हैं जो केवल मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं पर पाए जाने वाले रिसीवर्स से चिपक सकते हैं। चरण 4: शुद्धिकरण और फॉर्मूलेशन (Purification & Formulation) • क्रोमैटोग्राफी (Chromatography): इस प्रक्रिया द्वारा अशुद्धियों और खाली वायरसों को हटाकर केवल पूर्ण रूप से तैयार नैनो-कोडेड वायरसों को अलग किया जाता है। • स्टेबलाइजेशन: इसे एक बफर लिक्विड (जैसे फॉस्फेट-बफर्ड सलाइन) में मिलाया जाता है ताकि यह कम तापमान पर लंबे समय तक सुरक्षित रह सके। इसके बाद इसे वायल (शीशियों) में भरकर सील कर दिया जाता है। भाग 3: शरीर के भीतर वैक्सीन का सफर (In-Vivo Process) 1. इंट्रावेनस इंजेक्शन (IV Infusion): वैक्सीन को नस के माध्यम से सीधे रक्तप्रवाह में इंजेक्ट किया जाता है। 2. सर्कुलेशन: रक्त के जरिए दवा पूरे शरीर में घूमती है, लेकिन नैनो-कोडिंग के कारण इम्यून सिस्टम इसे नष्ट नहीं कर पाता। 3. मसल्स में प्रवेश: नैनो-लिगैंड्स केवल मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं के तालों को खोलते हैं और वायरस अपना जेनेटिक पेलोड कोशिका के केंद्रक (Nucleus) में छोड़ देता है। 4. स्थायी सुधार: CRISPR खराब जीन को डिलीट करता है और कोशिका का अपना तंत्र वहां नया स्वस्थ जीन फिट कर देता है। निष्कर्ष और भविष्य की राह बंटी कुमावत का यह "नैनो-इम्यूनो इवेसिव मॉडल" थ्योरी और लॉजिक के स्तर पर पूरी तरह परिपक्व है। चिकित्सा जगत में किसी भी नए जेनेटिक फॉर्मूले को मान्यता दिलाने के लिए इसे सबसे पहले इन-विट्रो (लैब में कोशिकाओं पर) और फिर इन-विवो (जीवों पर क्लिनिकल ट्रायल) के चरणों से गुजरना होता है, ताकि इसकी खुराक और सुरक्षा मानकों को अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर प्रमाणित किया जा सके। वैज्ञानिक शोध और फॉर्मूला दस्तावेज (Scientific Formula Document) परियोजना का नाम: नैनो-इम्यूनो इवेसिव जीन थेरेपी (Myo-Stealth Vaccine) मुख्य आविष्कारकर्ता (Concept Developer): बंटी कुमावत लक्ष्य: पीरियोडिक पैरालिसिस का पूर्ण और स्थायी उन्मूलन। 🧪 भाग 1: वैक्सीन का गणितीय और वैज्ञानिक फॉर्मूला (The Master Formula) इस वैक्सीन का मूल ढांचा चार मुख्य घटकों (Components) के मिश्रण से बना है। इसे हम एक वैज्ञानिक समीकरण (Equation) के रूप में इस तरह देख सकते हैं: \(\text{बंटी कुमावत Myo-Stealth Vaccine}=[A+B]\times [C+D]\) जहाँ प्रत्येक अक्षर एक विशेष तकनीक को दर्शाता है: • \(A\) = जेनेटिक कैंची (CRISPR-Cas9 System): यह CACNA1S, SCN4A, और KCNJ2 जीन के खराब हिस्से को काटने का काम करती है। • \(B\) = स्वस्थ डीएनए ब्लूप्रिंट (Healthy Donor DNA): यह वह सही कोडिंग है जो खराब कोडिंग की जगह लेगी। • \(C\) = आणविक डाकिया (MyoAAV Vector): यह वह हानिरहित वायरस है जो पेलोड (\(A+B\)) को अपने अंदर सुरक्षित रखता है। • \(D\) = नैनो-सुरक्षा कवच (Stealth Nanoparticle Coating): यह लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल (LNP) या PEG की परत है जो इम्यून सिस्टम को धोखा देती है और दवा को सीधे मांसपेशियों (Skeletal Muscles) तक पहुंचाती है। 🛠️ भाग 2: वैक्सीन बनाने की पूरी विधि (How to Manufacture the Vaccine) इस आधुनिक वैक्सीन को प्रयोगशाला में बनाने के 4 मुख्य चरण हैं: चरण 1: डीएनए और गाइड आरएनए का निर्माण (Designing the Payload) 1. सबसे पहले कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर पर CACNA1S, SCN4A, और KCNJ2 के खराब म्यूटेशन की मैपिंग की जाती है। 2. एक गाइड आरएनए (gRNA) तैयार किया जाता है जो खराब हिस्से का पता लगाएगा। 3. इसके साथ ही प्रयोगशाला में इन तीनों जीनों का बिल्कुल शुद्ध और स्

rows.title: Precision gene editing in infant neuroblastoma: a review of nanoparticle: enabled CRISPR/Cas9 therapies
rows.abstract: Infant neuroblastoma (NB), defined by diagnosis during the first year of life, represents a clinically heterogeneous disease spectrum ranging from localized tumours with favourable outcomes and a capacity for spontaneous regression, to high-risk metastatic disease requiring intensive multimodal therapy. In infants, treatment intensity is determined by disease stage, tumor biology, MYCN status, risk classification, symptoms, response to therapy, and metastatic involvement, particularly relevant to high-risk disease, consequently the potential toxicity of intensive treatment is specific to high-risk disease, as compared to favorable risk tumors which can be managed with surgery, reduced frequency techniques, or observations. Important determinations of neuroblastoma biology and prognosis are genetic alterations involving MYCN and ALK, but the predominately investigated field with therapeutic feasibility of targeting these changes with CRISPR/Cas9 is in preclinical neuroblastoma models rather than in infants. An investigational hypothesis is accordingly considered by their potential relevance to infant neuroblastoma rather than an established clinical application. The safe and efficient in vivo delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 components remains a major challenge, owing to cargo size, immunogenicity, and degradation, particularly within the delicate physiological environment of infants. This review emphasises the need for advanced delivery systems, focusing on the potential of nanoparticle-mediated approaches. Emerging preclinical findings support the feasibility of nanoparticle-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 delivery, although direct evidence in infant neuroblastoma remains limited. Importantly, the evidence for nanoparticle-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 therapy remains largely preclinical. Studies performed in general neuroblastoma models, non-cancer models, or adult cancers should not be interpreted as direct evidence of efficacy in infant neuroblastoma.

rows.title: Preclinical Safety Strategy for Ex Vivo Gene-Edited Autologous Cell Therapies in Sickle Cell Disease: An IND-Enabling Case Analysis
rows.abstract: Ex vivo gene-edited autologous hematopoietic stem cell (CD34+) therapies represent a distinct preclinical development category within cellular and gene therapy, in which a patient's own cells are collected, genetically modified outside the body, and reinfused as a single-administration product intended to provide durable clinical benefit. This article develops a complete, IND-enabling preclinical safety strategy for this product category in sickle cell disease, built on current FDA guidance for cellular and gene therapy products and for products incorporating human genome editing. The analysis departs deliberately from a conventional two-species small-molecule toxicology template, proposing instead a product-specific, relevant-species design: a disease-relevant immunodeficient rodent model supporting human cell engraftment, a conditional non-rodent analogue study bridging species-specific editing components, and an expanded human-donor cell panel addressing genome-editing specificity questions that animal models cannot resolve. The package addresses test-article supply expressed in viable edited cells rather than mass units, a genome-editing-specific genetic safety battery in place of conventional genotoxicity assays, integrated safety pharmacology monitoring embedded within in-life observations, and an illustrative 20-month program budget. Beyond this specific case, the article develops general principles for preclinical strategy design in novel biological modalities where conventional toxicology templates do not directly apply, and closes with recommendations for structuring the nonclinical section of an IND application for this product category. Keywords: ex vivo gene editing; autologous cell therapy; CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells; sickle cell disease; genome-editing safety; IND application; FDA cellular and gene therapy guidance

rows.title: Targeted delivery of gene replacement therapy for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas

THE PRECISION BIO-INTELLIGENCE FRAMEWORK FOR COMBATING MRSA AND PERSONALIZED MEDICINE FROM MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS TO GENE-EDITING THERAPIES A Unified Theory of Antimicrobial Resistance, Ultra-Early Detection, AI-Driven Drug Discovery, Personalized Genetic and Cellular Therapy, and Health Law
rows.abstract: The Precision Bio-Intelligence Framework for Combating MRSA and Personalized Medicine by Dr. M.K.A. El-Rakhawi (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23462676) establishes Precision Bio-Intelligence as a groundbreaking field integrating antimicrobial resistance, ultra-early detection, AI-driven drug discovery, genetic/cellular therapy, and health law through four pillars: (1) Biological Foundations exploring MRSA mecA/PBP2a resistance, Monod growth kinetics mu=mu_max*S/(K_s+S), and Cheng-Prusoff MIC_apparent=MIC_intrinsic*(1+[I]/K_i) for competitive resistance; (2) AI and Drug Discovery featuring cross-entropy loss L=-1/N*sum(y_i*log(p_i)+(1-y_i)*log(1-p_i)), Graph Neural Networks h_i^(l+1)=sigma(sum(W^(l)*h_j^(l))), and FICI synergy indices; (3) Genetic/Cellular Therapy covering high-fidelity CRISPR variants (SpCas9-HF1, eSpCas9, HiFi Cas9), Campbell Model phage-bacteria dynamics dB/dt=r*B*(1-B/K)-phi*B*P, dP/dt=beta*phi*B*P-d*P-phi*B*P, and Hill dose-response E=E_max*[D]^n/(EC_50^n+[D]^n); (4) Legal Frameworks addressing Myriad v. AMP (2013), EPC Rule 29(1) excluding natural gene patenting, GDPR genetic data protections, and WHO Global AMR Governance. Novel concepts include CRISPR-phages, AI-accelerated antibiotic discovery, and personalized pharmacogenomics. Applications span MRSA treatment, phage therapy, CAR-T immunotherapy, and global AMR stewardship. Protected under international copyright with multiple citation formats (APA, Chicago, MLA, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver).

rows.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Microleakage of Activatm Bioactive, Smart Dentin Replacement, Cention N and Conventional Glass Ionomer Cement In Class V Cavities – an in Vitro Study
rows.abstract: Context: Microleakage at the tooth–restoration interface may cause postoperative sensitivity, recurrent caries, and restoration failure. Newer bioactive restorative materials have been developed to improve marginal sealing. Aims: To compare the microleakage of ACTIVA™ BioACTIVE, Smart Dentin Replacement (SDR), Cention N, and Conventional Glass Ionomer Cement (GIC) in Class V cavities. Materials and Methods: Forty-eight extracted human maxillary premolars were randomly divided into four groups (n=12) and restored with Conventional GIC, ACTIVA™ BioACTIVE, SDR, or Cention N. After thermocycling and mechanical loading, specimens were coated with nail varnish, immersed in 2% Rhodamine B dye for 24 hours, sectioned buccolingually, and evaluated under a stereomicroscope at 30× magnification. Statistical Analysis: Microleakage scores were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test followed by the Dwass–Steel–Critchlow–Fligner post hoc test (p < 0.05). Results: Mean microleakage scores were 2.83 ± 0.39 for Conventional GIC, 0.58 ± 0.67 for ACTIVA™ BioACTIVE, 1.75 ± 0.75 for SDR, and 1.33 ± 0.78 for Cention N. Significant differences were observed among the groups (p = 0.0005). ACTIVA™ BioACTIVE exhibited the lowest microleakage, whereas Conventional GIC showed the highest. No significant difference was observed between SDR and Cention N. Conclusion: ACTIVA™ BioACTIVE exhibited the least microleakage and superior marginal sealing ability among the materials tested.

rows.title: A Smart, Cost-Effective Programmable Gas Flowmeter Retrofitted from a Glass Rotameter
rows.abstract: Programmable gas flowmeters with remote reading and control are increasingly needed in the era of automation and AI. However, commercially available options remain expensive, hindering their adoption. We therefore developed a cost-effective programmable flowmeter as a compact device based on a low-cost glass rotameter. This system consists of a reading unit (webcam + rotameter), a control unit (development board + stepper motor-actuated valve) using an open-loop pre-calibrated step-to-flow matrix, and a terminal interface. The side-view imaging of the glass rotameter avoids occlusion of the rotor by the scale, enabling reliable rotor identification using well-established algorithms. The flow rate is derived by mapping the normalized rotor position to the scale instead of recognizing the scale markings or numerals. Two terminal configurations are offered: USB-connected (PC + MATLAB) and embedded (Raspberry Pi + Python). The USB-connected configuration uses direct serial communication between MATLAB and Arduino for stepper motor step control, ensuring fast response and good compatibility. The prototype retains manual control and direct eye reading. Experiments demonstrated strong programmability, fast response (0.2 s), high accuracy (mean error < 3%), and stable reading (fluctuation < 0.5%). This cost-effective yet programmable gas flowmeter is expected to benefit gas sensor development and accelerate automation in fluid-related fields.

rows.title: Capital Allocation, Smart Glazing, and High Performance Applications in Advanced Glass
Cost-Effective Microfluidic-Based Transparency Switching Glass Visibility Control: Toward a Zero-Energy Smart Window Design.
rows.abstract: Smart window technologies are key to enhancing energy efficiency and user comfort in modern architecture. Traditional solutions like blinds and curtains face limitations in cost, maintenance, and space. This work introduces a microfluidic-based transparency-switching glass (MTSG), featuring microfluidic cavities filled with a liquid optically matched to the glass substrate. When filled, the cavities enable specular light transmission; in the absence of the liquid, internal wall roughening scatters light, rendering the cavities translucent. The MTSG achieves >85% transmittance modulation, ∼20 s switching time, with virtually no electrical power; if used, minimal power (<12 W/m2) is required, and only during switching. A unique curtain-rolling-like mechanism with the top portion maintained opaque and the bottom portion maintained transparent adds versatility and user-friendliness. This technology offers advantages over existing smart windows, including cost-effectiveness, use of readily available materials, and scalability for industrial production. Additionally, it addresses serious concerns related to power consumption, recyclability, and ease of operation. This design holds promise for smart visibility control in zero-energy buildings and sustainable architectural applications.
